c317c686d9e51e1b: SHAH ALAM: A babysitter who kicked a four-year-old boy hard enough to fracture his thigh bone has failed in her bid to overturn her conviction and five-year jail sentence.
The High Court here dismissed Nurdiana Lanonming's appeal after finding that the prosecution had proven beyond reasonable doubt that she abused the child while he was under her care in June 2023.

Judge Adlin Abdul Majid also dismissed the prosecution's appeal for a heavier sentence, ruling that the five-year prison term imposed by the Kajang Sessions Court was neither too harsh nor too lenient.

In her grounds of judgment dated Oct 7, Adlin said the boy, who was four years and 11 months old at the time, was particularly vulnerable and depended entirely on Nurdiana for his safety and protection.
"At such a young age, the victim did not have the physical ability to defend himself, the maturity to understand what was happening to him or the means to seek help on his own.
"While under the accused's care, the victim depended entirely on her for his protection, safety and welfare," she said.
She said Nurdiana had betrayed the trust placed in her by the boy's parents, who had entrusted their son to her care.
"Parents who entrust their children to the care of others do so with complete trust that their children will be well looked after and protected from harm.
"This trust is a responsibility. Those entrusted with it are duty-bound to act in the best interests of the child and must never become the source of harm to them.

"Unfortunately, the accused failed to fulfil this responsibility and trust. Instead, she betrayed the trust placed in her as a caregiver by injuring the victim, a child whom she was supposed to protect," she said.
The judge said such a betrayal of trust by a caregiver was a serious aggravating factor when determining an appropriate sentence.

Adlin also rejected Nurdiana's argument that there were inconsistencies in the victim's testimony, particularly during an interview conducted at the Child Interview Centre (CIC) about two months after the incident.
She said courts could not expect young children to give evidence with the same precision, fluency and structure as adults.

"A child's failure, at such a young age, to answer certain questions during an interview, whether due to shyness, fear, confusion or an inability to understand the questions, is something that can reasonably be expected.
"It does not, in itself, cast doubt on the child's testimony," she said.
According to the facts of the case, the boy's mother sent him to Nurdiana's house at about 6.20am on June 20, 2023.
He was healthy and able to walk normally when he arrived.
However, at about 10.51am, Nurdiana called the mother to inform her that the boy's right leg was swollen and that he could no longer walk.
The mother rushed to the house and took her son to Hospital Kajang, where doctors discovered a fracture of his right femur.

On the sentence, Adlin said the court had considered Nurdiana's lack of previous criminal convictions but found that this mitigating factor had to be weighed against the seriousness of the offence and the breach of trust involved.
"The five-year prison sentence, together with the other punishments imposed by the Sessions Court, is reasonable and reflects the seriousness of the offence committed by the accused.
"The sentence is neither manifestly excessive nor manifestly inadequate. Therefore, there is no reason for this court to interfere with the sentences imposed," she added.
Deputy public prosecutor Maizatul Munirah Abdul Rahman appeared for the prosecution, while Wan M. Razali Wan A. Kadir represented Nurdiana.

0a26e540e84a2bca: KUALA LUMPUR: Gerak Khas 2.0 actress Tisha Shamsir has issued a public apology to prominent producer Datuk Yusof Haslam, acknowledging that her involvement in an ongoing drug case has damaged his reputation.

Speaking outside the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate's Court following a case mention today, the 40-year-old actress — whose real name is Shanorbiah Shamsir Alam — expressed her deep remorse and asked for strength during this difficult time, Harian Metro reported.
"I want to apologise," she said. "I know this has, to some extent, tarnished the good name of my employer, Datuk Yusof Haslam. I am also deeply sorry to my family. I am praying for the best."
She added: "This is a heavy burden, but I accept it with an open heart and hope to stay strong."
The former Mentor Season 6 contestant admitted that the legal battle has disrupted her acting career and drawn harsh criticism online.
She urged the public not to judge her before all the facts are clear.
"It is normal for people to react. If ordinary people face criticism, someone in my position will naturally face even more.
"At the end of the day, we are all human, and none of us is immune to making mistakes.
"All I ask is that people on social media do not jump to conclusions so quickly," she said.
The court has scheduled Nov 10 for the next mention of the case.
Tisha was arrested alongside several others in early July during an 'Op Noda' vice raid conducted by the police in Kuala Lumpur.
05e9349cf4a4297f: SEPANG, Oct 8 — Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing departed for home this afternoon after concluding a two-day official visit to Malaysia.

Min Aung Hlaing was given a red-carpet ceremonial send-off and a guard-of-honour by the First Battalion of the Royal Malay Regiment, led by Capt Wan Muhammad Amirul Syafiq Wan Zamri at Bunga Raya Complex (BRC) of the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) here.
His delegation boarded a special flight at 2.10pm. They were sent off by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, who was the minister in attendance for the visit.
Min Aung Hlaing, who arrived yesterday, was accorded an official welcome at the Perdana Putra Complex in Putrajaya this morning.
After the ceremony, he proceeded to have a four-eyed meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, followed by a delegation meeting before attending a luncheon hosted by Anwar.

During the meetings, Malaysia and Myanmar agreed to strengthen bilateral ties, prioritise people-centric cooperation, and support Myanmar’s efforts to pursue reforms and policy adjustments aimed at addressing the country’s complex challenges.
The visit also resulted in Myanmar agreeing to accept the large-scale repatriation of its nationals at its own expense.

Speaking at a joint press conference, Anwar said more than 10,493 Myanmar citizens and personnel had so far been repatriated to Myanmar through flights and naval ships, with further repatriation to be negotiated between Malaysia’s Ministry of Home Affairs and its Myanmar counterpart.
He said the remaining Myanmar nationals would be repatriated according to the stipulated rules and procedures, subject to verification of their records.
Economic ties between Malaysia and Myanmar also showed significant potential, with bilateral economic activities increasing by more than 140 per cent year-on-year. — Bernama
d2be29eb26a2008b: KUALA LUMPUR: National Sports Day will go ahead as planned on Saturday, but poor air quality could force changes to some activities, including possible postponements.
Youth and Sports Minister Dr Taufiq Johari said organisers were closely monitoring the Air Pollutant Index (API) and would make a decision based on advice from relevant agencies.

"We are holding regular meetings with the Ministry of Youth and Sports through the National Youth and Sports Department, along with NADMA, MET Malaysia, and related agencies to assess current API levels.
"As of today, we are still proceeding with National Sports Day. However, we must also consider the advice and views from the committee that meets daily.

"If conditions do not permit on that day, contingency measures must be considered, such as outdoor programmes, Fun Walks, or runs," Taufiq said after launching Season 2 of the Jaguh Rakan Muda reality programme at Menara KBS in Putrajaya on Thursday.

He said logistical preparations for the National Sports Day programme, including the Larian Ria MADANI at the National Stadium in Bukit Jalil on Saturday, were almost 100 per cent complete, with programme scheduling also finalised.
Taufiq stressed that public safety remained the priority, particularly with the prevailing air quality and weather conditions.

"We want to ensure that members of the public attending National Sports Day do not face health risks. We also do not encourage young children or minors to participate in any outdoor activities, Fun Walks, or Fun Runs organised at present," he said.

He added that the ministry would continue monitoring weather and API conditions over the coming days while coordinating with state executive councillors, particularly in states such as Johor where API readings were high.
"If conditions do not permit, there may need to be postponements in certain areas," he said.
Taufiq said an official announcement would be made if activities in affected states had to be postponed, stressing that no decision had been made as of Thursday.
"There will be another meeting this afternoon to ensure everything remains safe and healthy," he said.

95b0d7c811325ea5: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia was ready to facilitate efforts towards lasting peace in Myanmar.
He said this after leading Malaysia's delegation at a bilateral meeting with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing, who is on an official visit to Malaysia.

"I stressed the importance of inclusive dialogue to make peace and reconciliation efforts in Myanmar a success, and expressed Malaysia's readiness to facilitate the process towards lasting peace," he said in a Facebook post.
Anwar said the discussions covered trade, the economy, energy and security, as well as efforts to tackle cross-border crime, which he said required coordination and shared commitment.
He said the well-being of the people had to be the priority.
"The welfare of the people must be a priority, particularly the protection of civilians and safe access to humanitarian aid for all affected communities," he said.
The repatriation of Myanmar nationals was also discussed, with an emphasis that it be carried out voluntarily, safely and with dignity, he said.

Anwar said Malaysia, guided by Madani diplomacy, would make full use of available mechanisms and channels, including through Asean, to strengthen bilateral relations and turn the understanding into concrete action.
"This is for the peace of Myanmar, the well-being of the people and shared prosperity in the region," he said.

dd756035d408d2e3: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP) is betting on electrification and green bunkering to cut emissions while strengthening its position as a major regional transshipment hub, as it deployed 52 electric prime movers in a major step towards decarbonising port operations.

Transport Minister Anthony Loke said decarbonisation was both an international obligation and a business imperative as the maritime industry moves towards the International Maritime Organisation's net-zero emissions target by 2050.
He said Malaysia also saw an opportunity to position its ports as green bunkering hubs as global shipping lines explored alternative fuels such as methanol, ammonia and liquefied natural gas.
"It's not only the ship, but at the port operations level, it is also important to reduce emissions," Loke said at the launch of PTP's complete electric prime mover fleet here today.
PTP is the first port in the country to deploy electric prime movers when 21 units entered service in August. The fleet has now expanded to 52 units.

Loke said the transition from diesel-powered equipment to electric prime movers would cut emissions from port operations, while stronger environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance would increasingly influence the competitiveness of ports.
"It's very important that we take the responsibility make our ports ESG compliance.
"When your ports achieve a certain level of ESG, that will of course give you better services, and better rankings in terms of the competitiveness of the port," he said.

He said the transport ministry's role was to establish policies and regulations to support the transition, including a regulatory roadmap for green bunkering being developed with the Australian government.

Loke said PTP's investment in the electric fleet was borne by the port operator and other port operators would need to follow as ESG requirements became increasingly important to international businesses.
PTP handled more than 14 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in 2025 and is targeting 16 million TEUs annually by 2029.
Loke said the PTP and Johor Port, ranked 11th among the world's busiest ports in the latest Lloyd's List ranking, behind Port Klang at 10th.
"PTP's scale and transshipment role also positioned Johor to attract more investment and develop a green bunkering ecosystem," he said.
f44914ea2454eeee: PETALING JAYA: Seorang pemandu e-panggilan di dakwa di Mahkamah Majistret Shah Alam atas tiga pertuduhan termasuk memandu bawah pengaruh dadah hingga menyebabkan kematian penumpangnya yang juga pelajar kolej swasta warga Maldives, Ahad lalu.
Tertuduh, Syafiq Ibrahim, 37, mengaku tidak bersalah selepas ketiga-tiga tuduhan dibacakan di hadapan Majistret Syafiq Sulaiman, lapor Berita Harian.
Mengikut pertuduhan, Syafiq didakwa memandu kereta Perodua Ativa di bawah pengaruh dadah jenis syabu sehingga menyebabkan kematian penumpangnya, Aamina Imeely Nazim, 22.

Lelaki itu turut didakwa menyebabkan kecederaan terhadap seorang lagi penumpang, Aishath Sara Nizam, 22, dalam kemalangan sama akibat pengaruh dadah dan didakwa mengikut Seksyen 44(1A)(a) APJ 1987.

f58a3dcc66d4ebcf: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Bagan Member of Parliament Lim Guan Eng has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to use Budget 2027 to deliver tangible economic relief, calling it the administration’s final realistic opportunity to win over voters before the next general election.
Lim proposed raising the personal income tax relief threshold to RM12,000 from the current RM9,000 to offset cumulative inflation, noting that the relief limit has remained unchanged for 17 years.

Speaking to media in Parliament ahead of the official Budget 2027 presentation, the former finance minister stressed that while a national Budget will be tabled in late 2027, its measures will not take effect quickly enough to influence the electorate before the government’s term expires.
Lim said that while he believed Anwar could still table the Budget before Parliament is dissolved, any attempt to win over voters would not be as effective as “it would be too late”.
“All our proposals are necessary. If not, I am worried this would be the last chance for the Madani government to make the Budget’s benefit tangible to the people,” he said.
“Yes, I believe he could still table another Budget, but I feel the impact will not be the same since it would be too late.”

Anwar acknowledged the economic strain on households in a social media post recently, stating that macroeconomic growth alone is insufficient and pledging that the upcoming fiscal plan will directly address cost-of-living pressures and distribute economic gains more equitably.

Malaysia’s current Parliament first convened on December 19, 2022, and its five-year term automatically expires in December 2027, requiring a general election to be held within 60 days unless Parliament is dissolved earlier.
Lim said there is typically a Cabinet meeting held before the tabling of the Budget, noting that in the past, last-minute additions have been made at such meetings.
“We suggest raising the personal tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000. The threshold for this relief has not changed for 17 years and if we account for inflation, RM9,000 in 2010 is now RM12,000.
In addition to personal income tax adjustments, Lim called for a RM1,000 increase in tax relief allocations for both education and healthcare expenses to assist middle-class families.

The DAP leader also advocated for targeted support for eldercare, appealing to the government to abolish the 8 per cent service tax recently imposed on private old-age homes to reduce the financial burden on caregivers.
642b194da5301dad: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia SEA Games Organising Committee (MASOC) is stepping up its oversight of preparations for the 2027 SEA Games to ensure spending and hosting arrangements remain within approved budgets and follow proper governance.

Youth and Sports Minister Dr Taufiq Johari said the organising committee was closely monitoring preparations as Malaysia enters the final year before hosting the biennial Games, with MASOC meeting regularly to ensure all processes run smoothly.

He was responding to concerns over financial management during the 2017 SEA Games, when an external audit conducted in 2019 uncovered several issues, including a RM9.56 million payment to a third-party vendor that was made without approval from the finance committee.

"Correct. Regarding SEA Games 2027, we are within the established timeline. Recently, we launched the 365-day or one-year countdown for SEA Games 2027," Taufiq said after launching Season 2 of the Jaguh Rakan Muda reality programme at Menara KBS in Putrajaya on Thursday.
"The MASOC meets regularly to ensure every process runs smoothly and well, adhering to proper governance and remaining within the set costs and budget."

Taufiq said the ministry wanted all hosting arrangements and implementation to comply with existing guidelines while ensuring that the focus of the Games extended beyond Malaysia's performance on the field.
"We want to make sure that all hosting arrangements and implementations follow existing guidelines and good governance.

"We also want to ensure that the SEA Games is not just about how many gold medals we can win or how prepared our athletes are. While that is very important, the overall hosting of the event is equally important," he said.

He said preparations would also focus on ensuring the opening ceremony, competition period and closing ceremony were delivered smoothly, drawing on Malaysia's experience in hosting major sporting events.

Taufiq added that the ministry would maintain close coordination with the state clusters involved in the Games — Sarawak, Johor, Penang and Kuala Lumpur — to ensure preparations remained orderly and on track.
He also said the government's allocation for sports in the 2027 Budget, to be announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Friday, would cover several areas.
"I can say our main budget focus is on sports development, athlete development, ensuring athlete welfare, youth Not in Employment, Education and Training (NEET), and youth skills," he said.
04c4568266c1882a: KUALA LUMPUR: Amendments to the Food Act 1983 are necessary to strengthen food safety controls and protect the public's right to safe food.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said existing provisions under the Act were no longer sufficient to address current food safety challenges and protect public health.
"The government faces various challenges in ensuring food safety in the country.
"Among the challenges are chemical contamination, including the misuse of pesticide and antibiotic residues, as well as the excessive use of food additives.

"The government also needs to strengthen its ability to detect emerging chemicals and pathogens influenced by climate change, as well as novel foods that require more comprehensive and up-to-date risk assessments," he said while tabling the Food Act amendment Bill for its second reading in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Dzulkefly said the increasingly complex food supply chain, involving multiple stages from farm to table, also posed challenges in ensuring food safety.
He said the amendments reflected the government's commitment to strengthening controls under the Act, including provisions on definitions, regulatory powers, enforcement and penalties.

"Among the proposed changes are stronger controls over food-contact materials and expanded powers for the health director-general to close premises that prepare, store or sell food that poses a health risk.
"The amendments would also empower the director-general to make public announcements without a court order and conduct field verification of overseas food facilities," he said.

Dzulkefly said other proposed changes included regulating the entry of food intended for sale but declared for personal use, revising and standardising definitions and the director-general's powers, as well as increasing fines and the maximum prison term.
He said the amendments would also strengthen enforcement activities by clarifying and enhancing enforcement powers.

According to the Bill, the amendments include Section 3 of Act 281, enabling the minister to authorise any public officer to obtain samples of food-contact materials that could affect consumers' public interest.
Clause 4 seeks to address advertising issues and empower authorised officers to summon any person with knowledge of the facts and circumstances of a case.

Meanwhile, Clause 9 seeks to introduce a new Section 8A into Act 281, empowering authorised officers to access recorded information, computerised data or digital data to conduct thorough investigations in line with the growth of online transactions.
Clause 13 aims to introduce a new Section 11A into Act 281 to provide for the closure of premises used to prepare or sell food containing substances harmful to health.
Other amendments include Sections 15 and 16, which respectively address labelling that fails to meet food standards and false labelling, to ensure they also cover food-contact materials.
e3f05097afafa46b: KOTA KINABALU: Noraidah Lamat told the Coroner's Court today that she hoped her daughter, Zara Qairina Mahathir, would regain consciousness and tell her what had happened to her.
Noraidah said she spent the night alone with Zara at the hospital, wondering what had happened after seeing blood on her daughter's head and legs.
"It was not about spending the night with Zara. I was more concerned about her condition.
"What actually happened? Why was Zara's head bleeding? Why were Zara's legs bleeding? Who did this to her?
"I really hoped Zara would regain consciousness, open her eyes and be able to tell me what actually happened to her," she said in response to questions from lawyer Shahlan Jufri.
Noraidah, the 82nd witness, was continuing her testimony before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan.
She said she stayed with Zara overnight at the hospital after her daughter was transferred to the neurological ward on the 10th floor.
The following morning, at 7am, a group of about three doctors made their rounds in the ward, accompanied by other medical officers.
She said the group included doctors she described as Chinese and Indian.
One of the doctors also offered words of encouragement that meant a great deal to her.
"The doctor said, 'Madam, you should make a police report about what happened to your daughter.'
"I asked again, 'Do I need to make a police report, doctor?'
"The doctor said, 'Make a police report for a case like this. Whether it takes a short or long time, we just have to wait for the outcome. It will take time,'" she said.
Noraidah said the doctor's words encouraged her to stay strong and keep fighting.
"Those words really encouraged me to stay strong and keep fighting," she said, describing the female doctor as relatively young and Chinese based on her facial features.
Zara was found unconscious on the ground floor of her school hostel on July 16, 2025.
She was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
Her remains were exhumed on Aug 9, 2025, before a post-mortem examination was conducted the following day at the Forensic Medicine Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
On Aug 20, 2025, five minors, identified by the pseudonyms Students A, B, C, D and E, were charged in the Court for Children with insulting Zara.
All five pleaded not guilty, and the trial is ongoing.

a21c07d3b7864c38: BUTTERWORTH: Three friends were fined a total of RM24,000 by the magistrate's court today after pleading guilty to threatening to kill a man and injuring his brother with sharp weapons last month.
Magistrate Aini Adilah Muhammad Faizal ordered Asyraf Hazlami Hussin, 30, Mohamad Kamarudin Hasan, 36, and Muhamad Muzzamir Bokhari, 36, to pay RM8,000 each after they admitted to two charges.

For the first charge, the trio were jointly accused of criminally intimidating Mohd Kufuan Aliff Ishak, 39, by holding a knife to his neck and threatening to kill him at Jalan Padang Benggali, Telok Air Tawar, at 10.15am on Sept 22.
The offence under Section 506 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, carries a maximum seven-year jail term, a fine, or both upon conviction.
The court fined each accused RM4,000 for the offence, or 10 months' imprisonment in default.
For the second charge, the three were accused of voluntarily causing hurt to Mohd Kufuan Aliff's younger brother, Mohd Rosmyzal Fammy Ishak, 36, using a parang at the same time and place.
The charge under Section 324 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, provides for up to 10 years' imprisonment, a fine, whipping, or any two of the punishments upon conviction.
The court fined each accused another RM4,000 for the second charge, or 12 months' imprisonment in default.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Nurfatin Fatini Shaiful Kamarul prosecuted, while National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Anas Hakimi Mat@Ahmad represented the accused.
In mitigation, Anas Hakimi asked for fines, saying the guilty pleas had saved court time and public funds.
He said Asyraf was single and worked at a clothing shop without a fixed income, while Kamarudin, a divorcee, worked as an excavator operator earning RM1,500 a month.
Muzzamir, also a divorcee, supported two children and earned RM1,500 monthly as a mechanic.
According to the facts of the case, the victims were in a car when the trio blocked their vehicle and approached them armed with sharp weapons.
One of the accused held a knife to Kufuan's neck, while another swung a parang at Rosmyzal, injuring his left arm.
The accused and the victims knew each other, and the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding.
3af6ffffd76085c9: KUALA LUMPUR: Winning the E-Commerce (Managed Service) category at the PIKOM Digital Excellence Awards 2026 validates a deliberate shift in how businesses handle online trade.

In an era where consumer discovery moves rapidly toward content, livestreaming, and affiliate-driven commerce, traditional marketplace management is no longer enough. Brands today require an end-to-end strategic partner capable of meeting buyers across every digital touchpoint.

Enter Commerce DotAsia Ventures Sdn Bhd (Commerce.Asia) Its company chief executive officer, Wilson Leong, said that the Group has built its market leadership by mastering this exact operational evolution. While many industry players handle isolated components, such as standalone logistics, isolated listing management, or basic checkout software — Commerce.Asia operates as a continuous, unified ecosystem. Its enterprise framework bridges brand distribution, warehousing, marketplace fulfilment, livestream content networks, and digital payments into a single, seamless engine.

Milk Diapers is a good example of building from zero to one, we helped grow the business from nothing to millions in revenue within a year, building the inventory, fulfillment and channel operations needed to support that scale. AKEMI shows the other side of our value by scaling an existing business further: by end-2025, its online business had grown approximately 30-fold from its 2019/20 level, through owning the full chain of distribution, marketplace strategy, warehousing, and fulfillment behind it.

For Leong, the value lies in taking much of that work off a brand's hands. "One of the biggest values we bring is simplicity, reducing the operational complexity a brand would otherwise have to manage on its own," he said. That allows brands to concentrate on their products while Commerce.Asia manages the operations behind online growth.

Payments are part of that picture. Commerce DotAsia Payments Sdn Bhd also won the Fintech category for its Unified Payment Platform, giving the group a second award. Registered with Bank Negara Malaysia as a non-bank merchant acquirer, the company helps merchants accept payments across their online sales channels.

Leong sees an opportunity for Malaysian companies to build these capabilities and serve brands across the region. "The opportunity ahead is for the whole industry to mature alongside consumer behaviour by building real, sustainable capability in social commerce rather than treating it as a trend," he said.
a72f7cda2711ac38: The ALBATROSS, a sailboat drone prototype developed by researchers at Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), lacks the aerial grace of its avian namesake. It doesn't so much fly as plummet – an unsettling start to a sea launch, more so because it's designed to spin like a maple leaf seed as it descends. The sailboat drone's rotation slows its fall and minimizes its impact with the water. This eliminates the engineering challenge of implementing hardware for two modes of mobility. There's no need for landing gear, actuators, or sensors to manage both flying and floating. Watch and download graphics and videos of ALBATROSS here. Developed by SUTD researchers Shane Kyi Hla Win, Danial Sufiyan, Brian Leonard Suhadi, Luke Soe Thura, Xinyu Cai, Wei Jun Ang, and Shaohui Foong, the ALBATROSS represents an achievement in both acronym construction and engineering. The Airborne Lander with Buoyant AuToROtating Sailing Sensor is described in a Science paper as a hybrid robotic system that combines a bio-inspired design for controlled aerial descent with autonomous sailing. Beyond the bio-inspired operation of the rigid wingsails for creating aerodynamic lift during descent and propulsion on the water, the ALBATROSS further cribs from nature's bag of tricks with a rudder that acts like a caudal fin – it moves side to side like a tailfin to generate thrust. And it does so with just three actuators and three primary sensors. Practically, the boat drone, which weights 1.107 kg, was built to fill the gap between expendable aircraft-deployed ocean instruments and floating robots deployed from ships or shore. Its light weight and adaptability make it well suited for rapid aerial deployment followed by energy-efficient persistence on the water, as might be required to monitor an oil spill or time-sensitive weather events. It is intended to be an alternative to large automated sailboats like Saildrone and Sailbuoy that may require ground- or ship-based management. And it has far greater deployment range than hybrid aquatic micro aerial vehicles: more than 100 km, compared to about 7 km for SailMAV, or so its makers claim. "Building on prior work on guided autorotation, ALBATROSS is designed to be released from an aircraft or UAV, passively enter autorotation for a controlled, low-impact water landing, self-right without actuation, and seamlessly transition into a wind-powered sailboat," the researchers explain. "Unlike many hybrid aerial-marine systems, ALBATROSS eliminates the need for aerial propulsion, complex mechanical reconfiguration, or active stabilization during the air-water transition and can sail back to shore at the end of a mission." The prototype takes flight amid a market doing the same. Last year, PwC's Strategy& consultancy issued a report [PDF] that forecasts a sea drone market worth €18.9 billion (~$21.2 billion) by 2030, based on a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) of 15.5 percent. f0f07e3065fc597d: BERLIN: Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) will launch a joint motion with the small far-left BSW party in a regional parliament calling for an end to military support for Ukraine, an AfD spokesperson said on Wednesday.

The motion, to be debated in the state parliament of Saxony-Anhalt next week, will have no immediate impact on Germany's foreign policy, which is exclusively the responsibility of the federal government in Berlin.

But it underscores the AfD's strong push for an end to German support for Ukraine and a restoration of ties with Russia, which have been largely severed since Russian forces launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
"This motion symbolises the desire for change," Ulrich Siegmund, the AfD leader in Saxony-Anhalt, said in a statement.

Siegmund led the anti-immigration AfD to its best-ever election result last month, topping the state election in Saxony-Anhalt but falling just short of the majority he would need to form the first-ever AfD government.
He has since been exploring potential cooperation arrangements with the BSW, which like the AfD has long opposed German support for Ukraine.

Siegmund said the party would use every opportunity to press the government of Chancellor Friedrich Merz "to finally campaign for an end to the war rather than its prolongation" and to use the money spent in Ukraine "for the people in our country."
In a message on the social media platform X, BSW founder Sahra Wagenknecht said Germany needed "a federal government that finally makes an effort to resume dialogue with Moscow."

The motion comes some two weeks after German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul spoke to his Russian counterpart Sergei Lavrov on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly in New York at a meeting that yielded no sign of any progress.

Lavrov was dismissive about the meeting in a press conference afterwards. Germany's Foreign Ministry said the meeting had reinforced Berlin's conviction that Moscow remains unwilling to negotiate either a ceasefire or an end to the war in Ukraine.

Merz visited Kyiv at the weekend to reaffirm Berlin's support for Ukraine, while German authorities have accused Russia of carrying out a series of hybrid and drone attacks in Germany, something that Moscow denies.

Iskandar Malaysia Studios (IMS) chief executive officer Rashid Karim said Malaysia already has an official co-production agreement with Australia.

a1c3f68d26e916f6: OCTOBER 8 — Last week, I had an unpleasant surprise at a petrol station.
Driving home to Klang from Kuala Lumpur, my Myvi was already on its last bar of fuel.
I stopped to refuel, only to realise that I had left my IC behind.
Without it, I could not access the subsidised petrol price and had to pay the full price.
Fifty ringgit barely brought the gauge to half a tank.
It was painful, but I understood the purpose of the constraint and its value to the country.
However, managing fuel quotas for transportation, particularly trucking, needs a different approach.
Trucks are not simply vehicles consuming diesel.
They are productive assets that move our economy.
Almost everything we use has travelled on a truck at some point, including food, construction materials, factory inputs, machinery, containers from ports and products being sent for export.
Without trucks, the supply chain stops.
Fixed diesel quotas already exist under the Subsidised Diesel Control System, or SKDS.
The industry’s concern now is the possibility of a vehicle-level arrangement where the quota allocated to one truck cannot be shared with another truck in the same company.
The industry’s concern is not simply about having a quota.
Operators understand why subsidised diesel must be controlled.
The bigger question is whether a rigid truck-by-truck, non-shareable quota is the right way to achieve that objective.
If the purpose is to prevent leakage, diversion and resale of subsidised diesel, then the control mechanism should focus on identifying misuse.
It should not unintentionally restrict the legitimate movement of goods.
A transport company does not operate every truck in the same way.
Its fleet may contain trucks of different ages, capacities, specifications and fuel efficiencies.
Some may be more suitable for certain customers, cargo or routes.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

The author argues that rigid, non-transferable diesel quotas for individual lorries could disrupt Malaysia’s supply chains by preventing transport operators from allocating subsidised fuel according to their fleets’ operational needs. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
One truck may be heavily utilised in a particular month while another may travel much less.
It is not the same as my wife and me using our respective ICs to fill the same family car after one of us has reached a personal fuel limit.
Trucking is a far more complex business, and trucks cannot simply be switched according to which vehicle has diesel quota remaining.
If a heavily utilised truck reaches its quota while another truck in the same company still has unused quota, what should the operator do?
Park the productive truck until the following month?
Move the job to another truck simply because it still has subsidised diesel available, even when that vehicle may not be suitable for the job?
That does not make operational sense.
There can still be strong controls.
One mechanism could be to verify the total kilometres travelled by a company’s fleet over a certain period, perhaps quarterly.
This would provide a reasonable ballpark figure for the operator’s fuel requirements.
Total kilometres travelled, fuel consumed, and the types of trucks operated would give the authorities a better picture of whether subsidised diesel is being used for legitimate operations.
Trucking also operates in one of the most visible and heavily regulated parts of the supply chain.
Trucks operate on public roads and must comply with requirements involving vehicle condition, inspections, permits, driver licensing, road safety, loading and other operating rules.
They are also subject to enforcement by different government agencies and authorities.
The concern is the cumulative effect.
One regulation by itself may appear reasonable.
Another requirement may also look manageable.
But when more and more operational restrictions are added, their combined effect can make it increasingly difficult and expensive for truckers to operate.
We should therefore be mindful about adding another operational constraint through a non-shareable diesel quota.
The planned third Port Klang terminal on Carey Island will strengthen the country’s future port and logistics capacity.
But bigger ports alone will not make Malaysia a stronger logistics hub.
A supply chain is only as strong as its weakest link.
Our logistics ambitions must therefore go hand in hand by making it easier, not harder, for SME trucking operators to do business efficiently.
Control the subsidy and prevent misuse.

But legitimate diesel consumption should be recognised for what it is, and any new operational requirements should be designed so that they do not unnecessarily constrain legitimate trucking activity.
* This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
f5b36819663871e9: KUALA LUMPUR: In a rapidly evolving digital landscape, true market leadership belongs to companies that can convert complex innovation into measurable business value. SRKK AI Bhd exemplified this principle by clinching the prestigious Artificial Intelligence (Business Transformation) award at the PIKOM Digital Excellence Awards (PDEA) 2026.

"We never just sell technology — anyone on the street can sell software," notes its chief executive, Yew Lip Sin. "Our true value comes from spending time understanding a client's deepest operational pain points. We map tech solutions directly to clear, measurable business objectives before implementation."
This focus on business impact is clearly demonstrated in their client achievements.

In one notable case study for a manufacturing client, SRKK AI modernised a legacy on-premises data setup into a scalable Microsoft Cloud architecture. The results were dramatic: processing time for critical research and development insights plummeted from 24 hours to just one hour — a 96 per cent operational efficiency gain — while saving the client over RM500,000 annually.

Serving mid-to-large corporate clients across manufacturing, logistics, retail, energy, and financial services, SRKK AI distinguishes itself through a holistic, end-to-end framework. Rather than offering isolated data or IT tools, the company integrates AI natively across every operational layer, including infrastructure, cybersecurity, ERP systems, and low-code applications.
SRKK AI is a strong proponent of digital adoption because avoiding it will result in higher implementation costs. In today's competitive economy, hesitation risks being left behind.
While targeted investments in intelligent automation allow businesses of all sizes to innovate, scale, and maintain long-term agility.

Fresh off its successful public listing, SRKK AI is accelerating its growth trajectory. The firm is currently working toward becoming an elite Microsoft Frontier Partner, certified to deploy specialised transformation engineering for advanced enterprise AI projects. By combining deep technical expertise with a commitment to ecosystem growth alongside industry bodies like PIKOM, SRKK AI is solidifying its position as a trusted driver of Southeast Asia's digital economy.
Our client achieved a 96 per cent operational efficiency gain while saving over RM500,000 annually.
fca55ec53f5c7b23: PETALING JAYA: A 27-year-old man was fined RM4,000 today for failing to comply with a police officer's instructions to stop tailgating a convoy escorting deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Kuala Lumpur traffic police chief Zamzuri Isa said the man pleaded guilty to the charge under Section 21(1) of the Police Act 1967 at the Kuala Lumpur magistrates' court.
The court also ordered him to serve eight months in jail if he failed to pay the fine.

The man, who was driving a Honda CR-V, was arrested yesterday after an incident at Km48.5 of the Shah Alam Expressway as Zahid's convoy was travelling from Kajang to Sunway Medical Centre in Subang Jaya.
Zamzuri said the man ignored warnings from a police outrider not to tailgate the convoy.
f2a103a3eb7f7eca: KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) today returned the investigation paper on the incident at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 to the police.

Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar confirmed that the move was to enable further investigation into the incident involving Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.
He said among the aspects requiring review was the authenticity of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, along with several other related matters, before any decision could be finalised.
"After reviewing the investigation paper, several aspects require further investigation to complete the file.
"The investigation paper will be returned to the police today for that purpose.

4a3fa8c2ae594443: LONDON: British foreign minister Ed Miliband said on Thursday its Consulate General building in East Jerusalem, ordered to close by Israel, would remain open as an independent and operational UK Mission, serving the Palestinian people.
Israel had ordered the British consulate in East Jerusalem to close on Thursday after London announced plans to impose sanctions on settlements in the West Bank.
Miliband said that having withdrawn a number of staff and families in recent weeks, it would now work to build up their presence again.
The deterioration in ties between the two allies had sparked speculation in Israel that Britain could respond to the closure by expelling Israeli diplomats in London.
"We will work in the coming months to build back up our presence, and we will not take reciprocal action while such discussions are underway and credible," Miliband said.

Britain's minister for the Middle East, Stephen Doughty, told Sky News that Britain was engaged in ongoing talks with the Israeli government, and that it deeply regretted Israel's actions in relation to its consulate.
"Our building remains open, our staff remain doing important work," Stephen Doughty told Sky News. "We retain a presence in Jerusalem ... and it is very important that that work is able to continue."

6e45cedf841cd948: KUALA LUMPUR: Pentech Solution Sdn Bhd is stepping up its expansion into artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and regional markets as it builds on two decades of growth in Malaysia.
The information technology solutions provider, which started operations in 2006 with 15 employees, has grown to nearly 150 employees.
It now has offices in Penang and Kuala Lumpur, and serves multinational, Malaysian and overseas customers.

Pentech Solution chief technology officer Darren Lim said the company's recognition at the PIKOM Digital Excellence Awards, where it won awards for Cloud Transformation and Managed Services, came at an important time as the company marked its 20th anniversary.
Pentech Solution Won Awards for Cloud Transformation and Managed Services
Lim said the recognition reflected the company's long-term efforts to build capabilities in cloud transformation and managed services, while earning customers' trust over the years.
Change quote to "Celebrating 20 years since Pentech" began operations in 2006 reflects how far we have come and what we have achieved.
Achieving ISO 27001 certification at the beginning of the year further demonstrates our commitment to internationally recognised standards.

"Our parent company Pentech Holdings Bhd's listing on the Ace Market in June made the occasion even more meaningful. Together, these milestones reflect our progress and position us for the next phase of growth," Lim told Business Times.
From traditional IT to cloud
Lim said, Pentech Solution began its cloud transformation journey in 2014, helping customers modernise their data centers and advance their digital transformation.

He said its managed services business provides round-the-clock support, including maintenance, preventive maintenance and proactive monitoring of customers' servers, applications, security and backup systems.
"Many customers face talent shortages and want their internal IT teams to focus on delivering business outcomes rather than day-to-day infrastructure management.

"By engaging a single vendor for services," he said. "end-to-end management and round-the-clock support, they can optimize costs, simplify accountability and free up resources for strategic priorities.
Pentech Solution has addressed this need through its managed services offering since 2020," he said.
Lim said the PIKOM awards recognised its strengths in cloud and managed services, as well as its growing AI transformation capabilities.
He said the company's ISO 27001 certification, obtained this year, assures customers that its processes, documentation, frameworks and security practices meet recognised standards.
"Customers already recognise Pentech as a trusted local company.
Our ambition is to become a world-class IT company by bringing industry best practices to customers in Malaysia," he said.
Pentech Solution has transformed from a traditional IT solutions provider into a technology business spanning cloud, AI and cybersecurity.
Drawing on that experience, the company now helps customers modernise their technology environments, adopt new capabilities and align digital transformation with business outcomes.
The company has also invested in upskilling and reskilling employees, moving some of its traditional IT workforce into areas including AI, digital transformation and cybersecurity.
Lim said the strategy was well-timed, as the Covid-19 pandemic accelerated demand for cloud technologies.
"During the Movement Control Order (MCO), everybody was working from home.
"So, whatever groundwork we had done in 2018 and 2019 started happening.
"Our growth began with cloud transformation in 2019 and accelerated significantly through 2022.
"Since then, we have expanded beyond cloud into cybersecurity, AI and managed services," he said.
Listing to fund next phase
With the business now moving further into AI and cybersecurity, Lim said the ACE Market listing was intended to provide the resources needed to transform the organisation further.
"One of the main reasons for our listing is to expand our cybersecurity business. We have acquired a new lot in Kuala Lumpur, beside our existing premise.
"We are going to establish our first local Malaysian security operations centre by a local IT solutions company," he said.
AI is another focus, although Lim said talent availability remains a challenge as customer demand increases.
He said Pentech Solution's AI strategy was focused on addressing specific customer needs rather than developing technology simply for the sake of having a product.
"Pentech Solution's AI solutions are supported by a structured process and framework designed to address customers' business challenges.
"As every industry has different AI requirements, we tailor each solution to the customer's specific needs.
"Through this framework, we help customers transform their operations and ensure that their investment in AI delivers measurable business outcomes and returns," he said.
Eyes Overseas Expansion
Beyond technology investment, Lim said Pentech Solution is also looking to expand beyond Malaysia, with Singapore emerging as a potential next market.
He said the company's multinational customers were an important factor in determining where it should expand.
"If you ask me, my next step most probably will be in Singapore because some of our existing Malaysian customers are there," he said.
Lim said the company had yet to finalise a concrete plan for Singapore, with strengthening its foundation in Malaysia remaining a priority.
He said that Pentech Solution's overseas business had already grown, with its contribution to revenue rising from about 1 per cent in 2022 to 4 per cent in 2025.
The company is managing cross-border services and strengthening relationships with existing customers as it considers potential next markets.

d12dbd05d82f46c8: KOTA KINABALU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's meeting with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing today does not constitute recognition of the country's government but is aimed at resolving the longstanding issue of Myanmar refugees in Malaysia.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the meeting reflected the government's use of diplomatic channels to address domestic concerns, particularly those involving Myanmar refugees.

"This meeting does not mean we recognise the Myanmar government. It is intended to find a solution to the longstanding issue of Myanmar refugees in our country," he said at the opening of the Inanam Sentral National Information Dissemination Centre (Nadi) here today.
Fahmi also expressed hope that the meeting would yield positive results, including facilitating the return of Myanmar refugees through proper channels.

"We hope the prime minister's meeting with the Myanmar President today will produce positive outcomes, allowing refugees from Myanmar's 19 ethnic groups in Malaysia to return to their country through proper channels and helping us address the issues we face domestically," he said.

Fahmi, who is also the government spokesperson, highlighted another important meeting scheduled for tomorrow after the tabling of the 2027 Budget, with discussions expected to cover efforts to strengthen bilateral ties and issues concerning Palestine.
"Let us await the outcomes of these two important meetings taking place today and tomorrow," he said.
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi is scheduled to make a state visit to Malaysia from Oct 9 to 10.

Dalam kejadian sekitar 7 pagi, Nor Daniel Fikri Norlizan, 11, dan Puteri Naufal Raisya, 8, dan abang mereka, Nor Daniel Aiman, 18, maut selepas bertembung dengan sebuah lori.
Julaiha berkata, kejadian menimpa tiga anaknya itu berlaku 200m dari kediaman mereka.

77622fa6862c98f1: PUTRAJAYA: Myanmar bersedia memudahkan proses penghantaran pulang warganya secara besar-besaran dan menanggung kos berkaitan, kata Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.

Beliau berkata setakat ini, lebih 10,493 warga dan petugas Myanmar telah dihantar pulang ke negara itu menerusi penerbangan dan kapal tentera laut, manakala urusan penghantaran pulang seterusnya akan dirundingkan antara Kementerian Dalam Negeri Malaysia dan kementerian berkaitan di Myanmar.

Anwar berkata Malaysia menghargai kesediaan Myanmar menerima kembali warganya, sambil menyatakan bahawa amat sedikit negara yang sanggup menerima penghantaran pulang rakyat mereka dalam jumlah besar dengan menanggung kos sendiri.

“Sangat sedikit, malah berdasarkan pengalaman saya, hampir tiada negara yang sanggup menerima penghantaran pulang warganya dalam jumlah besar dengan menanggung sendiri kosnya, seperti yang ditunjukkan Myanmar,” katanya.
Beliau berkata demikian pada sidang media bersama, sempena lawatan rasmi dua hari Presiden Myanmar Min Aung Hlaing, yang bermula semalam.
Mengulas lanjut, Anwar berkata baki rakyat Myanmar akan dihantar pulang mengikut peraturan dan prosedur yang ditetapkan, tertakluk kepada pengesahan rekod mereka.
Perdana menteri berkata Min Aung Hlaing turut memaklumkan bahawa antara 3,000 hingga 4,000 warga Myanmar yang kini berada di depot imigresen akan dihantar pulang ke negara berkenaan.
Beliau berkata pihak berkuasa berkaitan perlu mengesahkan kewarganegaraan dan rekod mereka, termasuk rekod jenayah sekiranya ada, sebelum proses penghantaran pulang dapat diselesaikan.
Anwar turut mengucapkan terima kasih kepada Myanmar atas kerjasama yang diberikan, khususnya dalam memudahkan penghantaran pulang rakyatnya.
“Saya sekali lagi ingin merakamkan penghargaan atas keterbukaan anda dan kesediaan untuk bekerjasama,” katanya.

Kedua-dua pemimpin turut membincangkan beberapa isu utama termasuk usaha menghantar pulang warga Myanmar daripada semua kumpulan etnik yang berada di Malaysia secara tidak sah, berasaskan prinsip sukarela, bermaruah dan selamat.
ff69bc87f894e843: WASHINGTON: The Trump administration has begun direct talks with Myanmar’s military-installed government, according to US officials and others familiar with the outreach, in a sharp reversal of Washington's efforts to isolate the country’s generals after the 2021 coup.

The US Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research, Michael Vance, played a leading role in the outreach, which has focused on shutting down scam centers that target Americans but could lead to broader engagement, including on Myanmar’s rare-earth mineral deposits, according to seven current and former officials and others familiar with the policy shift.

Vance joined talks with coup leader-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing in the capital Naypyitaw on Sept 15-16. The meeting was aimed at securing the release of American businessman Adam Castillo but also provided an opening for further engagement, four of the people said.
Last month’s meeting — the highest‑level contact since the coup — underscores a broader Trump‑administration foreign policy tilt away from democracy promotion toward transactional engagement.
The presence of Vance, who was confirmed as the State Department’s top intelligence official in August, and his ongoing role in US policy toward Myanmar have not been previously reported.

Min Aung Hlaing, the former military chief, remains under US sanctions for human rights abuses, including the 2016-2017 mass killings and expulsions of hundreds of thousands of Rohingya Muslims that Washington declared a genocide. Less than two weeks after Vance’s visit, Myanmar’s military conducted an airstrike on a crowded marketplace in Rakhine state, killing over 50 people and injuring scores more, according to United Nations human rights officials.
The State Department said it engages with all groups in Myanmar on issues affecting US interests and raises the need to cease violence and release political prisoners.
“You don't solve problems by ignoring them. You solve problems by addressing them,” spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a statement.

A spokesperson for the military-backed government did not respond to a request for comment. Min Aung Hlaing, who has cited electoral fraud to justify the coup and labeled his opponents as terrorists, is seeking international legitimacy for his nominally civilian government.
Current and former officials say Vance has met players from all sides of Myanmar’s complex conflict and helped shape the Trump administration’s policy toward the country.
Intelligence chiefs — such as Vance — do not typically steer policy because of concerns about compromising analytic independence.

“If you let policy dictate to intelligence, you can't be sure you're getting a real honest assessment of the facts,” said Richard Betts, an adjunct senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations who has consulted for US intelligence agencies.
Pigott declined to address Vance’s role but said the administration “operates as a team with the president as the lead.”

Castillo, a former head of the American Chamber of Commerce in Myanmar, was detained at Yangon airport on June 11 by Myanmar authorities on what his supporters have described as trumped-up charges. The US government has not commented on whether Castillo was wrongfully detained.

People familiar with the matter said White House, National Security Council and State Department officials held back-channel negotiations with Myanmar officials to secure his release. One person said Myanmar asked only "to have an official engagement at the right level with the US government" in return.
Castillo declined to comment beyond crediting President Donald Trump for his release.

The meeting builds on a June meeting between US and Myanmar officials in Tokyo also involving Vance, four people said. One of the people said officials from the Treasury Department, which oversees sanctions, the Department of Homeland Security, and the Pentagon took part.

A major focus of the US push is getting Myanmar's help shuttering scam hubsoperating on its territory that run romance and other frauds, which have scammed Americans out of billions of dollars. Two people familiar with the matter said the FBI has had direct contact with Myanmar’s authorities on cyber scams.
Researchers say many scams are run from areas under militia control, with some proceeds flowing to the military, raising doubts about whether Myanmar’s leaders are serious about enforcement.

US officials also discussed access to Myanmar’s massive deposits of heavy rare earths that are used in electric vehicles and wind turbines. US officials acknowledge obstacles: the deposits mainly lie in territory held by ethnic armies fighting Myanmar’s military government, and China, currently the main importer, could see any US role as a challenge.
Still, with Washington seeking to diversify supply chains away from China, Myanmar's deposits remain a recurring topic in conversations, the people said.
