Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi is scheduled to make a state visit to Malaysia from October 9 to 10. — Bernama
8c3e5076a961bfeb: PONTIAN: "I told them there was no need to go because school was closed today, but they insisted.
"So their older brother took them there to show them that the school was indeed closed. But on the way home, they were involved in the accident."
Julaiha Munaji, 42, said her three children were killed in a collision involving a motorcycle and lorry at Jalan Parit Haji Sirat here this morning.
She said she had told Nor Daniel Fikri Norlizan, 11, and Puteri Naufal Raisya, 8, they did not need to go to school as all schools in Johor were closed due to the haze.
However, she said the two children insisted on going, prompting their 18-year-old brother, Nor Daniel Aiman, to take them to school to show them that it was closed.
"I was told they turned back after finding out that the school was closed. They then headed home.
"The school is about 2km from our house. I was informed of the accident after a resident came to tell us that the motorcycle carrying my children had crashed.

"It happened only about 200 metres from our house. My husband and eldest child rushed to the scene, but all three had already been taken to Pontian Hospital," she said when met at her home in Kampung Parit Haji Sirat.
Julaiha, a mother of six, said her children had shown no signs of anything unusual and were cheerful before leaving home.
"Nor Daniel Fikri told me he wanted to play football. He even washed the shoes I had just bought for him.
"The three siblings were very close, and they slept with the family the night before the incident.
"Aiman was quiet, but he liked joking with me. They were all very close.
"Aiman was taken to hospital by ambulance but was pronounced dead there," she said.
Julaiha said Aiman had also helped her care for his younger siblings after she was involved in an accident four months ago while returning from taking them to school.
"He helped me a lot, including taking his younger siblings to school," she said.
Earlier, it was reported that the three siblings died after the motorcycle they were riding collided with a lorry at Jalan Parit Haji Sirat at about 7am.
The crash occurred on the first day of a two-day closure of schools in Johor following deteriorating air quality caused by haze.
c148119bd668fd8c: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 8 — Domestic port operators have been urged to accelerate their decarbonisation initiatives, including the adoption of electric terminal trucks (e-prime movers) for port operations, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke.
He said the shift towards greener practices aligns with Malaysia’s commitment under the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.

“Carbon reduction efforts at the port’s operational level must keep pace with the global shipping industry's transition, which is currently exploring the use of alternative fuels such as methanol, liquefied natural gas (LNG) and ammonia
“The use of electric-powered machinery, such as the e-prime movers implemented by the Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP), aligns with that objective.

“With that, I am confident that other port operators will follow suit. However, it still remains at the discretion of the port operators, as it involves investment and new assets on their part,” he told reporters after launching an electric terminal truck fleet at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas here today.
Also present were Johor Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh and PTP chief executive officer Mark Hardiman.

Loke said greater compliance with environmental, social and governance (ESG) standards would enable local ports to operate more responsibly while maintaining their competitiveness and strengthening their position in the global shipping industry.
“The Transport Ministry is committed to establishing policies and regulatory framework to support this green initiatives.
“We are also collaborating with the Australian government to formulate regulations regarding the supply of green fuel and to fine-tune standard operating procedures (SOPs) at ports,” he said.
He added that the transition to electric-powered machinery would also require supporting infrastructure, including charging stations and new safety protocols, to ensure smooth terminal operations.

Meanwhile, Loke commended the consolidation of PTP and Pasir Gudang Port under the ‘Johor Port’ brand, which he said had helped the combined port operations achieve a ranking of 11th among the world’s busiest ports.
He said Johor’s port facilities, comprising PTP and Pasir Gudang Port, handled more than 14 million containers annually.
“This achievement propelled its ranking to 11th place among the world’s busiest ports, placing it just behind Port Klang, which currently holds the 10th spot.
“PTP possesses immense potential to be developed into the nation’s largest green bunkering and transhipment hub.
“We hope this initiative will attract further investment and stimulate economic activity in the areas surrounding Tanjung Pelepas,” he said. — Bernama pic
31cf4ee7ceac9bb6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Digital Ministry will continue to strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI) training modules based on newly identified risks, including deepfake threats and the misuse of the technology.

Its Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the effort was being carried out through AI Malaysia Bhd, which also has an AI Safe initiative involving experts to examine security aspects and identify preventive measures against emerging technology threats.

“This is indeed something being monitored by AI Malaysia Bhd and it is a work in progress. We will ensure that each module is further strengthened whenever we identify new risks and the measures that can be taken to prevent people from falling victim to such risks,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

He said this in reply to a supplementary question from Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (PN-Kuala Krai) on measures taken by the government to address the risks of AI use among civil servants, as well as the misuse of the technology, including deepfakes, voice cloning, fake videos and AI-based scams.

He added that the training modules offered to various segments of society also included explanations of the risks associated with using new technologies, as well as ways to prevent users from falling victim to their misuse.

He said the aspect was also incorporated into the Executive Digital Leadership Programme (EDLP) and the use of Gemini Workspace in the public sector to ensure that civil servants understood the risks arising from the development of AI.

Responding to a supplementary question from Tan Hong Pin (PH-Bakri) on the role of AI Malaysia Bhd in expanding AI talent and skills development, particularly among youths, Gobind said the effort required collaboration among various parties, including the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Higher Education, industry and academic institutions.

He said AI Malaysia Bhd was responsible for identifying the country’s talent needs, compiling information on existing training modules and assessing their suitability to industry requirements and target groups.
The effort was also aimed at identifying existing training gaps so that new modules could be developed to meet the needs of people across various segments of society.

Gobind said the ministry was currently in the process of establishing a structure that would enable AI Malaysia Bhd to carry out the role comprehensively, while ensuring that AI talent development initiatives reached people who needed new skills. — Bernama
bb7acd45acb7c346: PETALING JAYA: Former health minister Dr Zaliha Mustafa today called for a national food safety alert system to allow consumers to quickly access information on unsafe and recalled food products.

Debating the Food (Amendment) Bill 2026 in the Dewan Rakyat, Zaliha (PH-Sekijang) said the proposed amendments would strengthen early action, including ordering premises selling food that could harm health to close immediately for a specified period.
She said the Bill would also strengthen requirements for food and food packaging materials to be recalled or withdrawn when a safety violation is discovered.

Questioning how information about such products would reach consumers quickly, she suggested that the health ministry provide an official channel for the public to access all food safety and product recall notices in one place.
"When a product is recalled, what mechanism will ensure that consumers know about it immediately?" she asked.

"I propose that the ministry consider a national food safety alert system for the public... (where) information such as the product name, affected batch, reason for recall, and action consumers need to take is made available immediately and easily."
Zaliha also asked whether the health ministry had sufficient resources, such as officers and laboratories, to enforce the expanded scope of the law.

She said the Bill would expand enforcement responsibilities, including taking food samples, accessing records, digital data for investigations, and verifying overseas food facilities when necessary to ensure the safety of imported food.
She said legislative amendments should be accompanied by stronger implementation capacity.
"In my view, amendments to the law must go hand in hand with a plan to strengthen capacity. A good law will not achieve its purpose if there is insufficient capacity to implement it," she said.
6e690990890249c0: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's stock market remains stable, supported by transparent government policies that have helped encourage foreign investment inflows into the country, the Dewan Rakyat heard today.

Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said stock market performance was influenced by various factors, including global geopolitical developments, which could sometimes trigger sharp declines.
"In the ups and downs of the capital market, we sometimes see share prices rise or fall due to various developments around the world.
"We are currently in a period of significant geopolitical changes, but Malaysia's stock market remains stable.

"We have not experienced sharp increases or sudden declines, and this stability, supported by the government's transparent policies, has helped encourage foreign fund inflows," he said in response to a question from Datuk Awang Hashim (PN-Pendang).
028e95fc5e96d177: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 8 — Several flights at Senai International Airport were delayed earlier today after haze caused poor visibility.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said at least five flights were affected, with aircraft unable to land because visibility conditions did not meet established aviation safety requirements.
As a result, he said several flights had to be diverted to Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and Changi Airport in Singapore.

“The situation was not just a matter of aircraft being unable to land, but it had also affected flights that had not yet departed from their points of origin as they were required to delay their schedules.
“Due to safety concerns, several flights had to be diverted as a priority.

“Even if a flight manages to depart, it is better for the aircraft to wait at the departure airport such as KLIA as it cannot land at Senai International Airport,” he told reporters at the launch of an electric terminal truck fleet at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas here today.
Also present were Johor Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh and PTP chief executive officer Mark Hardiman.
Loke also shared that his flight from KLIA to Senai, originally scheduled to depart at 6.45am, was delayed following instructions from Air Traffic Control (ATC).
He said all passengers had to wait inside the aircraft for nearly an hour and 45 minutes before it was allowed to depart at 9am after conditions improved.
“When I landed at Senai International Airport, there were indeed quite a number of passengers who were still stranded and had not yet departed.
“This was due to outbound flights that were affected by the delayed arrival of aircraft that had been diverted earlier.

“However, the disruption is temporary, and the situation is being closely monitored. I am confident that flight operations at Senai International Airport will be fully operational in the next two to three hours,” he said.

Earlier today, seven areas in Johor recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with Segamat recording the highest at 186, followed by Pasir Gudang at 180, Larkin at 178 and Tangkak at 171.
An API reading of between zero and 50 is classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are classified as hazardous.
56cedff460cb21b0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The government is confident of achieving its target of raising workers’ compensation to 40 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2030, in line with the aspirations of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), Deputy Economy Minister Datuk Mohd Shahar Abdullah said.

He said the government, through the Economy Ministry, would accelerate structural economic transformation towards a high-value economy driven by innovation, digitalisation, advanced technologies and knowledge-intensive activities to raise workers’ compensation.
“This structural transformation will create more skilled jobs offering higher wages.

“Implementation of national strategic initiatives such as the New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP) 2030, National Semiconductor Strategy (NSS) and National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) will attract more high-quality investment opportunities,” he said during a question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

He was responding to a question from Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman (PN-Bachok), who asked about the government’s strategy to raise workers’ compensation to 40 per cent of GDP by 2030, including measures to ensure wage growth keeps pace with productivity.
Mohd Shahar said workers’ compensation accounted for 33.9 per cent of GDP in 2025, up from 33.6 per cent in 2024, an increase of 0.3 percentage point.
He said the government would also consider expanding the Progressive Wage Policy to strategic sectors to ensure efforts to raise workers’ wages remain aligned with productivity growth.
“At the same time, the government is committed to raising the benchmark wage to RM3,500, and we are currently on track to achieve that target,” he added. — Bernama
e65a8f4c67cf15dc: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) emphasises four key approaches in addressing the issue of domestic violence: prevention, protection, intervention, and rehabilitation.

Deputy Minister of Women, Family and Community Development Lim Hui Ying said these approaches are crucial to ensuring victims receive appropriate protection and support, including after they have left the abusive situation.

“To strengthen the family institution, our programmes emphasise prevention. Subsequently, when an incident occurs, we focus on protection. We must have intervention measures in place, and another vital aspect is rehabilitation,” she said during the Kasih Lensa Keluarga podcast titled ‘With Love, Violence Ends!’ (*Dengan Kasih, Keganasan Terhenti!*), which was broadcast live on Bernama TV yesterday.
Lim noted that rehabilitation is essential to ensure that victims who have escaped domestic violence situations can rebuild their lives and become self-reliant.

Protection for victims also encompasses three forms of legal protection orders: the Emergency Protection Order (EPO), issued by the Social Welfare Department (JKM) without requiring a police report; and the Interim Protection Order (IPO) and Protection Order (PO), both issued by the courts and requires a police report.
She said domestic violence is not the way to resolve family conflicts instead, issues should be addressed through communication, mutual respect, and open discussion.
“If violence or a threat to safety occurs, victims must seek help,” she said.

Meanwhile, Lim said KPWKM is collaborating with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), government agencies, non-governmental organisations (NGOs), and the community to address this issue through a committee focused on data, education, capacity building, and protection.
She added that the community, including families and neighbours, must also play a role.

“Neighbours and family members need to shift their mindset and realize that this is not a matter of interfering in other people’s family affairs. Domestic violence is a crime; therefore, we can lodge a report,” she said.

The 24-hour Talian Kasih 15999 hotline serves as a channel for the public to lodge reports and seek advice as well as psychosocial counselling services, with complaints referred to the Social Welfare Department (JKM) for further action. — Bernama

* If you are experiencing domestic violence, the following hotlines offer free and confidential support: Talian Kasih at 15999 or WhatsApp 019-2615999 (24/7); All Women’s Action Society at 016-2374221/016-2284221 (9.30am-5.30pm); and Women’s Aid Organisation (WAO) at 03-30008858 or SMS/WhatsApp TINA 018-9888058 (24/7).
1fefe3b7b47cb49a: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are hunting the person who paid US$49,500 (RM202,250) to charter a private jet to traffic 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from Laos to the Philippines.

Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigators were working to identify the person who booked the aircraft, which was intercepted by Lao authorities at Luang Prabang International Airport on Oct 1.
He said investigations revealed that the aircraft belonged to a Malaysian private aviation company operating two jets available for charter.
3310658ecc2a8d3e: KUALA LUMPUR: Bekas Pengerusi Yayasan Bank Rakyat (YBR), Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin, mendakwa Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) melakukan salah guna kuasa ketika menjalankan siasatan berkaitan penyelewengan dan salah guna pelaburan bernilai kira-kira RM10 juta.
Beliau berkata, tindakan SPRM ketika melakukan penggeledahan dan penyitaan pada 30 Sept lalu di kediamannya dan abangnya, Mubarak Hussin juga disifatkan sebagai tidak profesional.

Katanya, sepanjang tujuh hari direman SPRM, hanya satu hari sahaja beliau disiasat berhubung isu dana RM10 juta YBR, selebihnya ditanya mengenai hal berkaitan politik yang tiada kaitan dengan siasatan.
Menurut Nazir lagi, siasatan berkait kes itu pernah dibuat SPRM pada 2022 namun beliau difahamkan tiada salah laku atau penyelewengan berkaitan perkara itu dikenal pasti.

“Saya dengan rendah diri merayu kepada Peguam Negara agar melihat perkara ini secara adil dan menyeluruh supaya saya tidak dijadikan kambing hitam atau alat untuk memenuhi kepentingan mana-mana pihak tertentu.

"Saya percaya masyarakat berhak mengetahui fakta sebenar dan saya bersedia memberikan kerjasama kepada mana-mana proses undang-undang yang sah,” katanya dalam sidang media yang turut dihadiri Mubarak dan peguamnya.

Mengulas dakwaan dana YBR RM10 juta yang didakwa diseleweng itu, Nazir menegaskan tidak ada satu sen pun wang yang hilang, sebaliknya pelaburan yang dibuat berdasarkan prinsip 'good governance', 'due diligence' serta tatakelola yang sewajarnya.
“YBR turut menerima pulangan hibah sebanyak RM1.85 juta daripada pelaburan tersebut. Pulangan hibah berkenaan dikreditkan terus ke akaun YBR setiap tiga bulan sepanjang tempoh pelaburan.
"Bagaimanapun, YBR telah menamatkan pelaburan tersebut pada November 2022,” katanya yang menjadi pengerusi yayasan itu dari 2020 hingga 2022.
Nazir juga menafikan dakwaan beliau menyalahgunakan kedudukan sebagai pengerusi YBR ketika itu dengan membuat pelaburan dalam sebuah syarikat milik abangnya.
Katanya, abangnya hanya salah seorang pelabur dalam syarikat tersebut selepas YBR membuat pelaburan.

Dalam sidang media itu, Nazir turut melahirkan rasa kecewa dengan SPRM yang membuat hantaran berkaitan penahanan beliau di akaun rasmi TikTok ‘SPRM Malaysia’ bersama selingan lagu 'penyamun' yang popular dalam filem 'Ali Baba Bujang Lapok'.

Katanya, sebagai sebuah badan penguat kuasa hantaran tersebut adalah tidak profesional kerana ia boleh menimbulkan persepsi kepada orang ramai sedangkan beliau belum didakwa atau dibuktikan bersalah di mahkamah.

Semalam, Ketua Pesuruhjaya SPRM, Abd Halim Aman, mengesahkan dua beradik tokoh korporat yang direman bagi membantu siasatan berkaitan penyelewengan dan salah guna pelaburan bernilai kira-kira RM10 juta dibebaskan dengan jaminan SPRM.

SPRM turut menyita 15 unit kereta mewah bernilai kira-kira RM31 juta, 12 unit motosikal berkuasa tinggi bernilai kira-kira RM5 juta, lima unit jam tangan mewah, tiga unit gelang tangan dan wang tunai berjumlah kira-kira RM30,000, selain membekukan dua akaun peribadi bernilai kira-kira RM2 juta.
2c516a25dc352c61: PETALING JAYA: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's meeting with Myanmar president Min Aung Hlaing today does not constitute recognition of the country’s government, but is aimed at resolving the long-standing issue of Myanmar refugees in Malaysia, says government spokesman Fahmi Fadzil.
Fahmi, who is also the communications minister, said the meeting reflected the government’s use of diplomacy to address domestic concerns, particularly those involving Myanmar refugees.
He also expressed hope that the meeting would yield positive results, including facilitating the return of Myanmar refugees through the proper channels.

"We hope the prime minister's meeting with the Myanmar president today will allow refugees from Myanmar's 19 ethnic groups in Malaysia to return to their country through proper channels, helping us address the issues we face domestically," he was quoted as saying by Bernama in Kota Kinabalu today.

Fahmi also highlighted another meeting with Egyptian president Abdel Fattah El-Sisi scheduled for tomorrow after the tabling of the 2027 budget, saying discussions are expected to cover efforts to strengthen bilateral ties and issues concerning Palestine.
El-Sisi is scheduled to make a state visit to Malaysia from tomorrow until Saturday.
dbc01932a536b398: LETTER: The 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was awesome. Congratulations to Max Verstappen for his first win of the 2026 season despite the rain, delays and rapidly changing conditions.
Sepang did not simply host the race. It became part of the drama.
The circuit is legendary. Its long straights, fast corners and wide racing surface give drivers room to attack, while its technical sections punish mistakes.
Heat, humidity, and the ever-present threat of tropical rain added to the challenge.
Put them together, and it is a nightmare for strategists, a great challenge for drivers and pure entertainment for spectators.
That may be the simplest way to describe the weekend. A crowd that still cares
The numbers tell one part of the story. A record 261,000 spectators attended over the race weekend, with 103,000 on race day, making it the largest crowd in Sepang circuit history.
The atmosphere became a defining feature of the weekend. Fans around the world praised the Malaysian crowd, while calls for Sepang to return to the Formula 1 calendar grew louder after the race.
And that is where the significance of this unexpected Grand Prix begins. Malaysia had not returned to Formula 1 through a long-term agreement or an elaborate comeback campaign.
Conflict in the Middle East disrupted the Bahrain race, and Sepang stepped in to replace it. For us, the opportunity goes beyond motorsport.
Formula 1 is one of the world's most powerful sporting platforms. Its global audience gives the host country an opportunity to showcase itself far beyond the circuit.
Malaysia should therefore look at the 2026 race not simply through the number of spectators who attended, but through what those visitors contributed to the wider tourism economy.
Visitors attending the race stayed in hotels, used local transportation, dined at restaurants, shopped, and, in some cases, explored destinations beyond Sepang.
Meanwhile, team social media channels and drivers' visits to Malaysian destinations extended the event's reach, showcasing Malaysia to a global audience beyond the F1 paddock.
In turn, F1 can become a tourism platform that encourages longer stays, wider visitor dispersal, and greater spending across the tourism value chain.
The race has already delivered international attention. The next challenge is to determine how much of that attention can be converted into lasting tourism and economic value.
Discussions are already underway to bring F1 back to Malaysia on a more permanent basis, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim opening the door to further consideration of Sepang's future.
As Malaysians, we will be very proud if the race returns to the circuit. A permanent return will come with significant financial and operational commitments.
If the 2027 calendar faces disruption, Sepang could once again serve as a potential Plan B, having demonstrated its readiness and capacity this year.
Another possibility is for Formula 1 to reserve two or three "wild-card" slots each season, allowing different countries and circuits to join the calendar periodically.
AKMAL ADANAN
Senior lecturer
Faculty of Hotel and Tourism Management
UiTM, Melaka

6477cfd4dc23f656: SARIKEI, Oct 8 — A new road linking Sare to Jalan Sentubu/Bukit Kinyau, costing approximately RM17 million, is expected to cut travel time to Sarikei town from 30 minutes to just 10 minutes.

Sarawak Deputy Minister for Urban Planning, Land Administration and Environment Datuk Len Talif Salleh said the 2.7-kilometre road would also provide an alternative route to Sarikei Hospital, thereby helping to ease congestion on the existing route.
He said the project, funded by the Rajang Delta Development Agency (RADDA), is scheduled for completion within 12 months.
He added that of the total cost, about RM1.4 million had been allocated for land compensation to some 20 affected landowners.

“This road will greatly benefit residents, as travel to Sarikei town will be shortened from about 30 minutes to 10 minutes,” he told reporters after the ground-breaking ceremony for the project and the presentation of compensation cheques to the affected landowners here yesterday. — Bernama
181be4796d092df4: KUALA LUMPUR: The Higher Education Ministry has assured that past disciplinary actions against university students will be dropped while existing laws are amended and a new higher education act is drafted.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir said serious offences involving students would remain subject to national laws.
He said the move aimed to remove restrictions on student freedom while harmonising conflicting university regulations.
"The ministry is taking all these aspects into consideration, and university management must also undertake the necessary coordination," he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.

He was responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Dr Ahmad Marzuk Shaary (PN-Pengkalan Chepa), who sought assurances that students would be free to voice criticism without facing disciplinary action under a proposed law replacing the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971.

The government previously directed universities and their student affairs departments to immediately drop disciplinary actions against students penalised solely for expressing opinions or criticising national leadership.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had said universities must remain platforms for open discourse and critical thinking, unconstrained by outdated regulations dating back to the 1970s.
626a65a269e59daf: KUALA LUMPUR: Dewan Rakyat deputy speaker Ramli Nor has given a government backbencher two days to refile a motion to debate the worsening haze, a day after the proposal was rejected by the lower house.
Ramli said that on a personal level, he agreed with Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who asked him to reconsider the motion, that the haze is an important issue.
"We face health-related issues, while schools are forced to close.
"And if the speaker agrees, I agree, too," Ramli said, referring to Johari Abdul.
Khoo's motion was rejected by Johari yesterday as the issue of haze had been addressed by natural resources and environmental sustainability minister Arthur Joseph Kurup on Tuesday.
Khoo had called for a debate on the haze, saying the situation was worsening and involved more than one ministry.
Apart from Kurup's ministry, Khoo said the foreign ministry was involved as well, as the haze was caused by fires in Indonesia.
He said he had received reports of Malaysian firms involved in the fires in the republic.
"This is a huge topic that requires a comprehensive explanation from several ministries, and I believe many MPs would debate this important issue," he said.
Thirty-eight areas had unhealthy air pollutant index readings as of 2pm.
b1ae715e89053cfd: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is strengthening its military presence and surveillance capabilities in northern Sabah amid increased United States military activities and the development of Philippine defence facilities on nearby Balabac Island, the Dewan Rakyat heard.

Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari said the armed forces would continue enhancing security readiness in Kudat, Pulau Banggi and Pulau Balambangan through stronger border security, improved intelligence capabilities and greater maritime and aerial surveillance.
He said the measures included strengthening intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities and maritime domain awareness through radar systems, drones and other monitoring assets.

"The Defence Ministry continuously monitors defence developments in the region, including the development of Philippine defence facilities and increased US military activities on Balabac Island, which is close to Sabah.
"The implications for national security and our strategic interests are continuously assessed," he said in response to a question from Datuk Ewon Benedick (GRS-Penampang).
Adly said Malaysia respected the sovereignty of other countries and their right to determine defence partnerships and cooperation arrangements.
However, he said Malaysia would continue strengthening its defence capabilities to safeguard national security.
"Meanwhile, Malaysia must ensure that its defence capabilities remain strong, credible and capable of responding to changes in the regional security environment," he said.

He said efforts to enhance Sabah's defence readiness would also include strengthening combat and support aircraft capabilities, command and control systems, as well as operational deployment facilities.

Adly said Malaysia was also adopting a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach involving the police, Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency, Eastern Sabah Security Command, National Security Council and Sabah government.
Defence cooperation with friendly nations would also be strengthened through intelligence sharing, joint training and military exercises.

He said Malaysia would continue using diplomatic channels, particularly through Asean, to maintain regional stability and prevent Southeast Asian countries from being pressured into choosing sides between major powers.
"Malaysia does not intend to engage in an arms race to match the military presence of other countries.
"However, strengthening our national defence remains a priority to ensure we are prepared for developments in the region," he said.

In his supplementary question, Ewon raised concerns over cross-border movements between Sabah and the southern Philippines, including potential security risks involving undocumented migrants and refugee communities.
He asked whether the ministry had assessed possible security threats linked to propaganda concerning territorial claims over Sabah.
Adly said national security challenges extended beyond conventional military threats to include smuggling, human trafficking and other non-traditional security risks.
He said these threats were continuously assessed through cooperation among defence and security agencies, including the Sabah State Security Council.

Meanwhile, Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman (PN-Sik) raised questions over whether Malaysia had received security assurances from the Philippines and the United States regarding military developments on Balabac Island.
He also sought clarification on plans to redistribute military personnel between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah and Sarawak.
Adly said Malaysia's defence planning extended beyond the 13th Malaysia Plan, with long-term strategies covering land, maritime and air security requirements up to 2050.

1141805fad8887a6: SINGAPORE, Oct 8 — Singapore Airlines will begin rolling out new closed-toe shoes for its female cabin crew in January, replacing the open-toed sandals that have long been part of its signature look.
The airline confirmed the change to The Straits Times, saying the new footwear follows a review focused on safety, comfort, support and operational needs.
The new shoes, developed with local footwear brand PAZZION, feature a closed-toe wedge design and will be worn throughout the flight rather than being switched with another pair at different stages.

Made from genuine leather, the shoes have thick lambskin insoles and incorporate SIA’s distinctive batik print, while their colours correspond with the crew member’s rank, including burgundy for Inflight Managers.
SIA said the closed-toe design offers added protection against spills and objects that could fall on crew members, with female cabin crew involved in the development process alongside PAZZION.
Several prototypes were also tested during actual flights before the final design was selected.
The change means female cabin crew will no longer need to alternate between footwear during a flight, with the new shoes to be worn during take-off, landing and the rest of the journey.

The outgoing sandals have been closely associated with the airline’s Singapore Girl image, featuring batik detailing and an open design that has traditionally complemented the crew’s painted red toenails.

They have also formed part of the visual identity surrounding SIA’s sarong kebaya, which was created by French designer Pierre Balmain for Malaysia-Singapore Airlines in 1968 before being adapted for SIA in 1974.

SIA introduced closed-toe slingbacks in 2001 following the crash of Singapore Airlines flight SQ006 in October 2000, which killed 83 people, although the airline said the footwear change was not linked to the accident and that its review had begun two years earlier.
Since then, crew members have worn the closed-toe shoes during take-off and landing before changing into the open-toed sandals for the remainder of the flight.
The new footwear will eventually replace both styles, with SIA saying the move is intended to make the uniform more practical and consistent.

79504fbb51d9fd1f: SINGAPORE: There might be "some restrictions" on outdoor activity such as entertainment during this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix, but not on the race, if the haze currently blanketing the city-state worsens, the motorsports governing body said on Thursday.

Singapore has been shrouded in smoke for weeks, with the air quality currently in the "unhealthy" range across the country, just a day ahead of the race weekend and during a busy week of conferences with regional, ​business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders descending on Singapore.

Despite the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in over a decade, the haze and poor air quality are not expected to threaten track activity or the staging of the F1 night race, said a spokesman from the Federation Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA).
"Air quality levels are being monitored by the relevant local authorities, and appropriate contingency measures are in place," said the spokesperson.
The FIA did not give a threshold for when plans affecting entertainment and other outdoor activity would be activated.
The spokesman said they were following recommendations from local authorities and working closely with them to safeguard the health of F1 teams.
Singapore's National Environment Agency and tourism board did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
On Wednesday evening, the environment agency's haze update said: "Under the prevailing southeasterly to southerly winds, smoke haze from these areas may continue to drift towards Singapore."
In 2019, when haze was similarly in the "unhealthy" range during the Singapore Grand Prix, organisers had first aid help on standby and made N95 masks available to those who needed it.
25021032d69b3ce5: SHAH ALAM: An e-hailing driver was charged in the magistrate's court today with driving under the influence of methamphetamine, causing the death of a 22-year-old Maldivian passenger on Sunday.

Muhamad Syafiq Ibrahim, 37, was accused of driving a Perodua Ativa under the influence of methamphetamine, which caused him to lose control of the vehicle and resulted in the death of private university student Aamina Imeely Nazim.
He pleaded not guilty to a second charge of driving the same vehicle under the influence of methamphetamine, causing him to lose control and injure another passenger, 22-year-old Aishath Sara Nizam.
Syafiq pleaded not guilty to the charges framed under Section 44(1)(a) and Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Section 44(1)(a) carries a jail term of between 10 and 15 years and a fine of between RM50,000 and RM100,000 upon conviction.
Section 44(1A)(a) carries a jail term of between seven and 10 years and a fine of between RM30,000 and RM50,000 upon conviction.
Syafiq further claimed trial to a third charge of driving without due care and attention, resulting in a collision with another vehicle and causing injuries to Aishath.
The charge under Section 43(1) of the same act carries a fine of between RM5,000 and RM10,000 and a jail term of up to 12 months.
All three offences were allegedly committed at 8.40pm on Oct 4 along the Damansara-Puchong Highway near the Puchong Selatan toll plaza, heading towards Puchong.
Before magistrate Muhammad Syafiq Sulaiman, the accused, handcuffed in the dock, said he understood the charges and the penalties.
He was brought into the courtroom after being held under a four-day remand order. He sat on a bench guarded by a traffic policeman before his case was called.
Several of his family members were present in the public gallery and followed the proceedings.
The magistrate asked Syafiq whether he held a valid driving licence, to which he replied that he did.
Deputy public prosecutor Alia Anisa Khairus Masnan urged the court to set bail at RM10,000 with one surety for each charge.
Lawyer Rohan Singh sought a lower bail amount, saying his client was supporting his wife, who is a housewife, and their two children, aged three and four.

"He earns about RM2,000 a month as an e-hailing driver. Apart from supporting his immediate family, he also financially supports his 63-year-old mother, who suffers from asthma and requires medical treatment," he said.
Rohan said his client was not a flight risk as he had a permanent address and had cooperated with the police throughout the investigation.
"He did not attempt to abscond. His wife is the proposed bailor and she will ensure that he attends future court proceedings," he said.
The magistrate granted Syafiq bail of RM3,000 for each charge, totalling RM9,000 with one surety.
The court also ordered the suspension of Syafiq's driving licence pending the outcome of the case.
The court fixed Dec 8 for mention.
Subang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat had said the crash occured when the driver of the Ativa struck another car when approching the toll plaza's RFID lane.
The impact caused the Ativa to spin before overturning in the middle of the crash.
He said one passenger suffered minor injuries while the other was trapped and died at the scene.

309e339241525d7d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Ministry of Works (KKR) is taking seriously the 13 findings in the 2026 Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) on Phase 1 of the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway (LPB) project and will use them to strengthen project delivery and the implementation of other Federal government development projects.

“Project delays were caused, among others, by the change in the implementation method from the Project Delivery Partner (PDP) model to the conventional method, the Covid-19 pandemic, land acquisition issues, utility relocation and contractor performance.

d1fd6f4ff815f204: PETALING JAYA: The Penang High Court has allowed Senator Dr RA Lingeshwaran’s appeal against the Butterworth sessions court’s dismissal of his defamation suit against Urimai chief P Ramasamy.

"Instead, the High Court granted an injunction barring Ramasamy from repeating or republishing the statements that were the subject of the suit.

In the defamation suit, sessions court judge Zulhazmi Abdullah ordered Lingeshwaran to pay RM15,000 in costs, finding that Ramasamy had successfully raised the defences of fair comment and qualified privilege.

The suit concerned two remarks by Ramasamy in a Malaysiakini article published on May 2, 2024, following a public debate over opening Universiti Teknologi Mara’s cardiothoracic surgery postgraduate programme with the National Heart Institute to non-Malays to address a shortage of heart surgeons.

In his ruling, Zulhazmi said the first remark was not defamatory but amounted to criticism made in the course of political debate. He said the second remark was capable of being defamatory as it touched on Lingeshwaran’s professional standing as a doctor, but was protected by fair comment and qualified privilege.

Zulhazmi also said Lingeshwaran failed to prove that Ramasamy acted with malice, noting that Lingeshwaran was the only witness to testify and no other witnesses were called to establish actual or inferred malice.

d57e2289cc1a2c57: ICANN has revealed the applicants for new generic top-level domains (GTLDs). As The Register reported in August, this is just the second time ICANN has accepted applications for GTLDs, strings like “.com” or “.net”. For years, only ICANN could create and operate GTLDs. The governance body changed that policy and in 2012 allowed over 1,200 new GTLDs. The organization decided to repeat the process this year and on Wednesday announced it received 1,615 applications. A process is now under way to confirm those applications are viable. ICANN has made information about all of the applications available in a searchable form here along with a downloadable list that The Register has pored over to bring you news of the following applications. OpenAI wants 15 GTLDs, among them .chatgpt and .agi – the latter likely the acronym for artificial general intelligence. Six other entities also want that string. The AI upstart also wants .mcp, which probably refers to the open source Model Context Protocol. Google bid for this GTLD, too, as have three other entities. The Big G, through its subsidiary Charleston Road Registry, is in an eight-way tussle to score .api. It has applied for over 30 new names, most pertaining to its products. Anthropic wants only its own name and .claude. Microsoft is another that hopes for just a pair of names: .copilot and .msft. Meta will have to fight another contender to control .superintelligence, but is the only entity trying to claim .wearables. 13 entities hope to claim .agent, with Meta and Google among the contenders. Salesforce wants its own name, plus .force, .slack, and .tableau. An outfit named Fomalhaut Exploration wants .intel. That could be Chipzilla acting through a third party, or the beginning of a legal tussle. Three contenders want to be the home of .drone, while nine are fighting over .brand. Ten applicants want to build their own .hub, while two hope to take GTLDs to .mars. Seven operators hope to run .official, the kind of domain that brands buy defensively so they end up with [companyname].official before someone cynical nabs the name. North America was home to most applicants – 864 – followed by 506 Europeans, 218 from Asia Pacific, 16 from Africa, and just 11 from Latin America and the Caribbean. When multiple parties apply for the same GTLD, ICANN first applies a “community priority evaluation” process that tries to find the most appropriate home for a string. If that fails, rights to the GTLD go to auction. All applications must be decided by November 17, aka String Confirmation Day, after which successful applicants can start the work to establish a registry for their new GTLDs. Readers will likely be able to register domains using the new GTLDs next year. ®

a912218cfd7b5474: KUALA LUMPUR: Timbalan Speaker Dewan Rakyat Ramli Mohd Nor meminta Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka) mengemukakan semula usul membahaskan isu jerebu selepas usul berkenaan ditolak pejabat speaker semalam.

ef4432f9def2eeb0: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 8 — Myanmar is prepared to facilitate the repatriation of its nationals on a large scale, with the country ready to bear the associated costs, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.

“Very, very few, hardly any country in my experience, are willing to accept this repatriation in large numbers at their own expense, as you have shown in Myanmar,” he said in his remarks during a joint press conference here today in conjunction with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing two-day official visit that began yesterday.
Anwar said the remaining Myanmar nationals would be repatriated according to the stipulated rules and procedures, subject to verification of their records.

23c3b815c915c310: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 8 — Myanmar’s leader Min Aung Hlaing said Thursday that migrants from his war-torn country held in Malaysian detention centres will be returned home “as soon as possible”.

79f2ea78dde4eae1: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Lima penerbangan yang dijadualkan mendarat dan berlepas di Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Senai (LTAS), Johor Bahru terjejas pagi ini berikutan jarak penglihatan rendah akibat keadaan jerebu.

Beliau berkata demikian kepada pemberita selepas Majlis Pelancaran Armada Lori Terminal Berkuasa Elektrik di Pelabuhan Tanjung Pelepas (PTP).
Menurut Loke, penerbangannya dari KLIA ke Senai yang sepatutnya berlepas 7.15 pagi turut terjejas apabila ditangguhkan selama satu jam 45 minit sebelum dibenarkan berlepas.

5f71f4261682f1d7: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 8 — Malaysia and Myanmar have agreed to further strengthen bilateral relations by focusing on people-centric cooperation, including trade, investment, education, agri-food, energy, healthcare and capacity building.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said both countries committed to enhancing collaboration while taking into account issues that needed to be addressed.
“We have had excellent relations for a long time, but of course recent developments have somewhat blocked that sort of progress. So I think our interest is, of course, to enhance this collaboration.

“We, of course, are reminded of the Asean mechanism, but we also understand that the President and your government have made a lot of efforts not only to enhance bilateral relations but to have the necessary reform policy changes and adjustments in your own country,” he said at a joint media conference with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing, here today.
Economic ties between Kuala Lumpur and Yangon according to him, had shown significant potential, with bilateral economic activities increasing by more than 140 per cent year-on-year.
“Which is quite to me impressive, in terms of our economic ties and potential,” he added.

Anwar said Malaysia had conveyed its views openly and frankly, while appreciating Myanmar’s openness in sharing its own perspectives, as such the approach was important to further fortify bilateral relations.
“Of course, as we know, in any country, issues are complex, multi-ethnic with a wide range of differences, it is a process that we need to understand and respect,” he said.

On Myanmar’s domestic situation, Anwar said Malaysia had conveyed its concerns on issues including democratic reforms, while acknowledging the complexity of the country’s situation as a multi-ethnic nation.
He said Yangon’s commitment to engage with all parties to avoid further escalation of violence was among the policy positions that Malaysia welcomed.
“When I met you in Bangkok after the earthquake, you made certain policy statements which were quite remarkable to me.
“For example, our field hospitals should allow any person without discrimination and that you will continue your policy to engage with all parties to avoid further escalation of violence.
“Of course, I welcome that and convey to my colleagues, not only here, but also in Asean. But how you do it, the mechanism of course is up to you as a leader of the country,” he said.
Anwar described Min Aung Hlaing’s visit as important not only for Malaysia and Myanmar but also for the region.

“With this visit, I would say that we and our part in Malaysia, we’ll do whatever is possible to make sure that we enhance this collaboration and ultimately take Myanmar as part of our community of nations without prejudice and particularly in the context of Asean.
“But for now, bilaterally between Malaysia and Myanmar, it should be the high par,” he said. — Bernama
55645cc85d463dff: NEW DELHI: India on Thursday hit back at claims by tech billionaire Elon Musk that unnamed "oligarchs" had blocked his Starlink entry to protect their monopolies, with officials saying government regulations were "fair".

The potential launch of Starlink, which provides high-speed internet access to remote locations by low Earth orbit satellites, has seen fierce debate in India over issues ranging from predatory pricing to spectrum allocation.
In March 2025, Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms said it had signed a deal with Musk's SpaceX to offer Starlink's satellite internet service to its customers.
But it has yet to launch and on Wednesday, Musk said in a post on X that it was being "blocked".
"Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people," Musk wrote.
"You can guess who they are... This is a crime against the people of India!"
India's ministry of communications said Thursday that the government had a "fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services".
It made no mention of Musk, but only a post "being circulated in social media regarding the fairness of India’s regulatory framework for satellite communication services".

It added telecom licences had been granted to satellite services "as part of its commitment to enable provision of satellite communication services in India", without specifying the names of the companies.
"Security assessment as part of this process is currently under way in respect of all the three licensees," it said.
"As and when this process is completed for a licensed entity, it may proceed to the next step".

e8c76508cab844e7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is reviewing the implementation of a dedicated 30 per cent quota for specialist training via the Federal Training Award (HLP) for medical officers serving in Sabah and Sarawak.

Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said this measure reflects his commitment to uplifting, honouring, and recognising the sacrifices made by all medical officers serving in those two states.

“Currently, we have 1,650 HLP slots available, therefore, approximately 30 per cent or 500 places are being specifically allocated to those serving in Sabah and Sarawak,” he said during the Ministers’ Question Time session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

Dzulkefly was responding to a question from Suhaizan Kaiat (BN-Pulai) regarding the high rate of medical officers failing to report for duty in Sabah and Sarawak following the expiration of the reporting deadline for 4,255 officers yesterday and the measures the Ministry is taking to address the issue.
Regarding the number of medical officers who reported for duty, he noted that 337 out of the 527 individuals offered positions reported in Sarawak, while in Sabah, the figure was 336 out of 528.
“Overall, the percentage of medical officers who reported for duty in Sabah and Sarawak was 63 per cent of the total placements offered.

“Although this figure shows a slight improvement compared to the ‘no-show’ or failure-to-report rate of 42 per cent recorded between 2020 and 2025, the rate has only decreased by five per cent this time,” he said.

Dzulkefly said factors such as being far from family and a preference for working in urban health facilities were among the reasons medical officers declined permanent appointment offers for placements in those two states.
According to him, medical officers also hold the view that career prospects are less favourable if they serve in rural and remote areas.

“Officers wish to care for their parents and siblings and want to be close to their spouses. They also face health issues, as well as logistical challenges, personal financial constraints, and high relocation costs.

“Furthermore, there is a perception that opportunities for pursuing specialist training are limited if one is posted to Sabah and Sarawak, alongside concerns regarding career progression and the chances of transferring back to the Peninsula or their home regions,” he said.

To encourage medical officers to report for duty in Sabah and Sarawak, Dzulkefly said the Ministry of Health (MOH) has improved the placement process for permanently appointed medical officers by upgrading the eHousemen (e-Placement) system.

“In addition, officers are eligible to receive a transfer allowance at a 100 per cent rate covering meal allowances, hotel accommodation costs, travel fares, and various other benefits that were previously unavailable due to the transition from contract to permanent employment status.
“Upon transferring back to their home regions, medical officers are also eligible for a disturbance allowance equivalent to one month of their substantive salary,” he said.

Regarding whether the government would consider phasing out contract positions in the future, Dzulkefly stated that the matter would be announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in the near future.

“My goal since returning to helm the Ministry of Health (MOH) for the second time has been to end this contract service arrangement, and this matter has already been taken into consideration,” he said. — Bernama

Skim yang menawarkan 50% geran serta penangguhan bayaran pembiayaan sehingga empat tahun itu membolehkan mereka menampung kos pembersihan tanah, pembelian benih dan pengurusan kebun sementara menunggu pokok baharu mengeluarkan hasil.
Ia adalah inisiatif kerjasama Kementerian Perladangan dan Komoditi, Lembaga Minyak Sawit Malaysia (MPOB) dan Agrobank bagi membantu pekebun kecil persendirian melaksanakan penanaman semula.
Bercakap kepada FMT, pekebun kecil dari Sabak Bernam, Norlinda Mokhtar, 45, berkata modal menjadi antara kekangan utama untuk menanam semula kebun sawit kerana kos yang perlu ditanggung agak besar.

“Namun dengan skim ini, penangguhan bayaran sehingga tahun kelima dan hanya perlu membayar 50% daripada modal memang sangat membantu dan tidak membebankan kami,” katanya yang mengusahakan kebun seluas 1.97 hektar.

Seorang lagi pekebun kecil dari Sabak Bernam, Mahfudz Hasan Anuar@Annuan, 62, berkata proses tanam semula semakin penting apabila pokok sawit berusia lebih 20 tahun mula mengalami penurunan hasil selain berdepan ancaman penyakit Ganoderma.
Mahfudz, yang hampir 30 tahun mengusahakan sawit, berkata TSPKS 2.0 turut memberi peluang kepadanya menggunakan teknologi dan benih baharu bagi meningkatkan produktiviti kebun.
“Penangguhan bayaran serta penambahbaikan syarat seperti pemansuhan keperluan penjamin bagi warga emas amat meringankan beban,” katanya.
Beliau turut menanam tanaman selingan seperti labu dan pisang bagi menjana pendapatan sementara menunggu pokok sawit baharu mengeluarkan hasil.

Manfaat sama dirasai pekebun kecil di Sabah, Farid Rizwande Mohammad Johan, 38, dari Kunak, yang berkata skim itu membolehkannya mengusahakan semula kebun warisan keluarga yang terbiar selepas pemergian bapa saudaranya.
Menurutnya, kos membersihkan dan meratakan tanah serta membeli anak benih sebelum ini terlalu tinggi sehingga memaksanya menangguhkan rancangan menanam semula.
“Apabila MPOB memberikan maklumat mengenai TSPKS 2.0 dan menghubungkan saya dengan kontraktor berdaftar, barulah saya mampu melaksanakannya,” katanya.

Sementara itu, Abdul Karim Abdul Rani, 63, yang mengusahakan kebun di Perak dan Selangor berkata agihan dana secara berperingkat di bawah skim itu membantu menampung kos sementara menunggu pokok baharu mengeluarkan hasil.
“Bantuan gabungan geran dan pembiayaan ini membolehkan kita menebang pokok tua yang tidak lagi produktif.
“Cuma sebagai pekebun kecil, kami berharap pembiayaan ini dapat ditukar kepada geran penuh pada masa akan datang bagi mengurangkan kebergantungan kepada pembiayaan bank,” katanya.

57d9b776788f6da9: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 8 — The Federal Court today allowed Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and the Attorney-General (AG) leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision allowing the Malaysian Bar to commence a judicial review challenging the prosecution’s decision to discontinue the Yayasan Akalbudi corruption case.

A three-man bench comprising Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah and Federal Court judges Datuk Nordin Hassan and Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali held that the case raises novel constitutional issues of public importance that require clarification and final determination by the Federal Court.

Delivering the unanimous decision, Justice Hashim said the case concerns the threshold for granting leave to commence a judicial review when the AG’s prosecutorial discretion under Article 145 (3) of the Federal Constitution is being challenged.

He said the High Court had applied a two-step threshold based on its interpretation of the Federal Court’s decision in the Sundra Rajoo case, while the Court of Appeal, on the other hand, applied a single-leave test.
“And the test must be applied with greater discipline, caution, and restraint when it involves the AG’s prosecutorial power under Article 145 (3),” he added.
Justice Hashim said both Ahmad Zahid and the AG had met the threshold requirement under Sections 96 (a) and 96 (b) of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 for leave to be granted.
He said the court allowed four questions of law proposed by the Deputy Prime Minister and dismissed one, while both questions of law proposed by the AG were allowed.

One of the questions is whether, in cases involving challenges to a decision by the Public Prosecutor in exercising his powers under Article 145 (3) of the Federal Constitution, the two-step threshold must be satisfied before leave to commence a judicial review can be granted.

Another question is whether, when a criminal court made an order of discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) pursuant to the public prosecutor’s application under Section 254 (1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, the remedy for judicial review lies against the Public Prosecutor’s application during the subsistence of the DNAA order?
On May 7, this year, the Court of Appeal granted the Malaysian Bar leave to commence a judicial review to challenge the AG’s decision on September 4, 2023, to halt proceedings against Ahmad Zahid.
The Court of Appeal had overturned the June 27, 2024, High Court’s decision, which rejected the Malaysian Bar’s application for leave to commence the judicial review.

Ahmad Zahid, who is the second proposed respondent in the judicial review proceedings, subsequently filed an application on May 25 this year seeking leave to appeal to the Federal Court. AG Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar filed a separate leave to appeal application.

In the judicial review application, the Malaysian Bar is seeking a declaration from the High Court that the decision by then-High Court Judge Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah (now a Federal Court judge) to grant Ahmad Zahid a DNAA on 47 criminal breach of trust, corruption and money laundering charges related to the Yayasan Akalbudi funds is null and void.
The High Court granted the DNAA after the prosecution informed the court that the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) intended to halt proceedings against Zahid to scrutinise new evidence.

During the proceedings, Ahmad Zahid was represented by a team of 11 lawyers led by Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik, while Senior Federal Counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly@Arwi and Federal Counsel Imtiyaz Wizni Aufa Othman appeared for the AG.
The Malaysian Bar was represented by a team of lawyers led by Datuk S. Ambiga and Steven Thiru. — Bernama

0f69c4a48fae1c71: SINGAPORE, Oct 8 — Air quality across Singapore remained in the unhealthy range today, with 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) readings above 100 in all five regions.
The 11am readings were 112 in the north, 111 in the south, 122 in the east, 159 in the west and 142 in the central region, according to The Straits Times.
The PSI, which measures a 24-hour rolling average of six key air pollutants, is considered unhealthy when it reaches between 101 and 200.
Meanwhile, hourly PM2.5 readings, which indicate current air quality and are used to guide immediate outdoor activity, were elevated in the west at 67 and central region at 57.

Readings in the north, south and east remained within the normal band at 44, 33 and 49 respectively, while an hourly PM2.5 reading between 56 and 150 indicates an elevated concentration of fine particles.

The hazy conditions are expected to continue through the October 9-11 Singapore Grand Prix, although a Formula 1 spokesperson had earlier told ST: “There is absolutely no risk to the event and the conditions where the event is taking place are not at any level of concern.”
A Singapore GP spokesperson said it would work with relevant agencies to assess the situation and make decisions if the haze affects visibility, public health or operations.
The organisers also have a contingency plan developed with stakeholders and government agencies for various scenarios, including haze, with N95 masks to be made available at the event if necessary.

The National Environment Agency (NEA) advises healthy people to reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor activity when the 24-hour PSI is in the unhealthy range, while vulnerable groups including pregnant women, children and people with chronic lung or heart conditions should minimise or avoid such activities.

In its October 7 haze advisory, NEA forecast that the situation would worsen, with the PSI expected to remain within the unhealthy range for the first time since daily advisories began on September 4.

NEA said moderate to dense smoke plumes from southern Sumatra and smoke haze from hotspots in Kalimantan were drifting towards Singapore, with prevailing south-easterly to southerly winds expected to continue carrying the haze towards the city-state.
The PSI first crossed into the unhealthy range on September 4, when it reached 101 in central Singapore, while the highest reading this year was 167 in the central region on September 29.

The recent haze marked the first time since October 2023 that Singapore’s PSI had reached unhealthy levels, amid earlier warnings of increased haze risk between June and October due to warmer and drier conditions associated with El Nino and the Indian Ocean Dipole.
Some experts have forecast that the haze could persist for longer this year because of the “Godzilla” El Nino event, which could bring less rainfall and higher temperatures in October and November.

The Meteorological Service Singapore said strong El Nino events tend to delay the end of the dry season across much of southern Asean, with the transition in Singapore expected only in late October or early November, later than in the previous two years.

4c75baed558f55ac: The global building boom of power-hungry data centers is straining electrical grids, causing greater reliance on energy from polluting fossil fuels. Christina Delimitrou, a newly tenured associate professor at MIT, is fighting this environmental threat by rethinking how the computer servers and networking equipment inside those data centers operate.  She and her group apply machine learning to make large-scale data centers more efficient, secure, and reliable. They redesign outdated cloud computing systems, develop methods to manage shared hardware resources, and create streamlined server architectures.  These advances allow data center operators to coax more computational power out of existing hardware. “If data centers are not utilized to the best of their capabilities, then they will burn much more power than they need to meet growing user demand,” says Delimitrou, the KDD Career Development Associate Professor in Communications and Technology in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) and a member of the Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL). “There is a lot of bloating, especially on the software side of these systems. If we can remove that bloating in a way that doesn’t compromise performance, then we won’t need to build as many new data centers.” She also harnesses AI to help programmers find and fix problems in cloud-based applications, like music-streaming services or video conferencing systems. This eliminates application downtime that hampers performance and drains computational resources. “By managing resources more effectively in the cloud, the end user gets more predictable performance from the application running on their smartphone,” she adds. Mathematical beginnings Delimitrou grew up in a midsized town within the vast plains of northern Greece. Her early interest in math and science was sparked, in part, by the ancient history of her homeland, where Euclid and Pythagoras studied mathematical problems more than 2,000 years ago.  “In Greece, there is a long tradition of geometry,” she says. She also drew scientific inspiration from her parents. Her mother worked as a chemical engineer and her father as a pharmacist — and both encouraged their daughter’s innate curiosity. Her early affinity for math led Delimitrou to study computer engineering at the National Technical University of Athens, even though she didn’t know much about the field. She quickly gravitated toward courses that focused on the applied science of engineering. For her diploma thesis — a project all students complete during their fifth and final year of study — she studied resource management in a computer when multiple applications are running at once.  “A lot of the challenges I was looking at then would get much harder if, instead of a single system, you had 100,000 of these systems. That was a problem that piqued my interest,” she says. Seeking to make a bigger impact as a researcher, Delimitrou pursued a graduate degree at Stanford University. She began tackling inefficiencies in cloud computing systems and large-scale data centers, which was a rapidly growing area of research.  Through that work, Delimitrou and her research mentor, Christos Kozyrakis, the Leonard Bosack and Sandy K. Lerner Professor of Engineering, realized many large computing systems were underutilized. “You would expect, with all the demand for these systems, that they should be running close to 100 percent capacity. But we found that most were running at only about 15 percent capacity,” she says. “This is not a resource-efficient or sustainable way of scaling these systems.” Applying AI To push that utilization closer to 100 percent, she began investigating machine-learning solutions to streamline cumbersome computational processes. Machine learning could automate resource management operations in the cloud, identifying solutions that developers might miss on their own. “Applying machine learning to solve a large-scale system problem was a novel approach at the time. It was a bit risky because people had not yet shown that these techniques would work,” Delimitrou says. “But empirical approaches require a lot of expertise, and the scale of the system is so large that it is difficult for users to manage. This is why machine learning is often the best solution.” After earning her PhD, Delimitrou continued this line of work as an assistant professor at Cornell University. One tool her group developed, Seer, uses deep learning to anticipate and prevent problems in web applications before they happen. This averts widespread slowdowns that may occur if a developer tries to fix a problem manually.    As she delved deeper into cloud computing, Delimitrou observed that cloud applications were changing. Developers were now splitting applications into smaller pieces to spread across multiple servers, which increases the speed of deployment. “But the servers were not built for this new style of application design. So, I rethought some of my earlier work to build machine-learning systems for this new class of applications,” she says. To tackle these new challenges, she found herself collaborating more often with faculty members who had different software and hardware expertise. Those collaborations opened exciting new research areas. A few years later, she decided to join MIT because of the opportunity to collaborate with researchers at the top of their fields in hardware and software engineering. She became an assistant professor in EECS in 2022. Creative approaches At MIT, Delimitrou also enjoys the teaching aspect of her role. One of her favorite courses to teach is 6.191 (Computation Structure), a popular undergraduate class with about 350 students each semester.  While it’s challenging to keep the course material fresh when the field constantly evolves, she strives to inspire creativity in her students. “I want the students to learn how to think and learn on their own. Part of that involves shifting away from formulaic assignments and making classes more open-ended. I’d rather give the students something to make them think more deeply,” she says. In the lab, a creative mindset helps Delimitrou and her team identify novel solutions to problems in cloud computing that others might overlook. For instance, she extended prior work on debugging problems in cloud applications to encompass not just errors in the code, but also security issues that can make user data vulnerable to hackers. She also uses AI to redesign software systems so they better fit the capabilities of existing hardware. “One of the challenges when it comes to applying AI to these systems is that the AI is not interpretable,” she says. “A lot of the work we are doing now involves adding explainability into these AI tools so people can get useful feedback from the system.” That not only helps developers ensure AI is giving the right answer, but also provides insights into how to design systems better in the future. She finds that studying these large-scale cloud computing systems is becoming more challenging because tech companies that operate data centers use proprietary hardware, unlike the commodity equipment of early cloud computing days, as well as software systems that can’t be accessed by academic teams. A solution that works in the lab might not work in the real world. To that end, Delimitrou and her group create clones of proprietary systems and applications. One tool they developed, called Ditto, mimics an application’s structure and performance characteristics, enabling a wide range of studies. She expects her work to continue shifting as machine-learning models become more advanced, opening new possibilities to boost application performance and hardware efficiency. “But you still have to use AI carefully. While it can greatly accelerate the application development side, we still need to audit it and be especially careful about how these models are applied so we don’t lose the ability to gain insights out of the solutions AI is giving,” she says. Outside the lab, Delimitrou enjoys spending time with her husband and 1-year-old daughter. While she doesn’t have as much time for hobbies these days, she also enjoys gardening and building an electrical toy train track for her daughter, as well as playing classical piano and painting nature scenes. She became interested in painting at Cornell, where she would often paint the many waterfalls near the campus.  Whether she is working in the garden or painting, Delimitrou says she finds spending time outdoors to be a relaxing escape from the technical nature of her work, but also an important reminder of the role her research plays in sustainability.

82cf8609adf38b7f: RIO DE JANEIRO, Oct 8 — Thousands of people joined a student march Wednesday in downtown Rio de Janeiro to protest against election favorite Flavio Bolsonaro and the prospect of the far-right’s return to power in Brazil, as the campaign for a runoff election swung into action.

Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, came out in front in Sunday’s first-round election, sending shockwaves through Brazil’s left which is scrambling to claw back votes ahead of an October 25 runoff.

With drums, fireworks, and spirited chants, thousands of students spilled into downtown Rio de Janeiro declaring “Never Again Bolsonaro” and calling for votes for leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

“I’m here because I believe in democracy. Because I’m scared,” said Alice Carneiro, 25, an administrator in maritime shipping, crying as she expressed fears about a possible backlash against her wife, who is transgender.

Protesters evoked life under Jair Bolsonaro, who was in office from 2019 to 2022 and is remembered for his government’s handling of the Covid pandemic, which he dubbed a “little flu” and which claimed more than 700,000 lives in Brazil, the second-highest death toll in the world after the United States.
“I remember my family’s lives being at risk during the pandemic…I remember the vaccine denial,” said Carneiro.
The march was strikingly more crowded and animated than Lula’s rally at the same spot on Friday before the election, after a campaign many had criticised as lacklustre.
Fears of social spending cuts
Flavio Bolsonaro has vowed sweeping budget cuts, using a pair of scissors to echo the chainsaw of libertarian Argentine President Javier Milei, whose economic reforms he has praised.
Brazil is battling soaring public debt exacerbated by high interest rates, and the election result saw the Sao Paulo stock exchange rally to record highs.

Amid uncertainty over what cuts Flavio will make, protesters recalled those made by Jair Bolsonaro to federal universities, research scholarships and the government-subsidised Farmacia Popular programme, which provides free or discounted medicines.

“It’s pointless for me to pass the entrance exam only to end up at a university that lacks funding,” said Emmanuel Araujo, 19, who is preparing to take university entrance exams and described the rise of the far-right as “very sad.”
Iara Pinheiro, 16, who voted for the first time, carried a placard reading: “No to the father, no to the son.”
“I am a Black woman and I think we’ll lose our rights if things continue the way they are and we elect Bolsonaro again. I think we will end up losing our democracy.”
Some protesters expressed concern about Flavio Bolsonaro’s plans to seek amnesty for his father, currently serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup after his 2022 election loss.
“Granting amnesty for coups gives the green light for new coups,” read another placard.
Several other pro-democracy rallies are planned in the coming days.
Campaign reset
Both Flavio Bolsonaro and Lula are shaking up their campaigns to prepare for the runoff.

Flavio Bolsonaro has focused on building coalitions and doubled down on his plans to shrink the state and modernise the tax system. He also promised to use the right’s new dominance in Congress to make constitutional reforms.

Lula, who at almost 81 years old is seeking a fourth term in office, has hit reset with a major focus on social media — where the right has long held the advantage — posting a video selfie on Wednesday for the first time.
“Come on, folks, let’s hit the streets; let’s go talk to people,” he said in the video posted to Instagram and TikTok. — AFP
